The merged route carries `.AddQuickCreateSourceAccessFilter()`, which master's task 030 says makes the 'caller hold Read on the record context' (OfficeEndpoints.cs:1517). Its WithDescription (:1513) also says Matter and Project use 'the caller as a load-bearing owner (an unresolved caller is refused with 403 and no row is written)'. So the waiver both under-states the control and misdescribes owner attribution for Matter and Project.
verified.recommended_fix: If the first finding's fix credits QuickCreateSourceAccessFilter, Rule A will see the route as gated and this waiver can be deleted, since it is Permanent and no rule flags redundant Permanent waivers. Otherwise, rewrite it to describe the record-context read gate and the load-bearing owner rule, and keep the note that CREATE privilege is not checked.

The claim is accurate. The staleness comes from the merge itself: our waiver text was written against our side's route, and master changed that route underneath it.

The waiver text comes from our side only. `git show HEAD:tests/Spaarke.ArchTests/RouteAuthorizationGuardTests.cs` has the quickcreate Permanent waiver at line 618. `MERGE_HEAD`'s version of this file has no Office entries at all (a grep for quickcreate or office/ returns nothing). The merged copy at RouteAuthorizationGuardTests.cs:631-638 is word-for-word our pre-merge text. It still says "There is no pre-existing resource to authorize" and "the write runs on the app identity with best-effort owner attribution."

2. The route that text describes changed on master. In our pre-merge registration (HEAD OfficeEndpoints.cs:1194-1207) the only filters are RateLimit, Idempotency and OfficeAuth. The merged route (OfficeEndpoints.cs:1510-1517) comes from master and adds `.AddQuickCreateSourceAccessFilter() // word-add-in-r1 task 030 - caller must hold Read on the record context`. QuickCreateSourceAccessFilter.cs:37-40 and :81-153 show that RecordCreationService reads a caller-named source record app-only. The filter checks the caller's Read right on that record over OBO and fails closed. So there is now a pre-existing resource on this route, and it is authorized. The waiver says the opposite and never mentions the filter.

3. "Best-effort owner attribution" is now wrong for Matter and Project. The merged WithDescription (OfficeEndpoints.cs:1513, from master) says the caller is a load-bearing owner and an unresolved caller gets 403. The code agrees:
   - RecordCreationService.cs:231-241 (Matter) and :337-347 (Project) return `RecordCreationFailureKind.OwnerUnresolved`.
   - OfficeService.cs:2716 maps that to 403.
   - OfficeEndpoints.cs:1878-1879 says Matter and Project are load-bearing and only Invoice stays best-effort.

4. The waiver cannot simply be deleted. FilterMarker (RouteAuthorizationGuardTests.cs:1834-1844) credits only `*AuthorizationFilter`, `AddEndpointFilter<*Access*Filter>`, `AddEntityAccessFilter(` and `AddJobOwnershipFilter(`. `.AddQuickCreateSourceAccessFilter()` matches none of these, so Rule A still sees the route as ungated and the Permanent waiver is still load-bearing. That confirms the defect is the waiver's text, not its existence.

5. This is not one of the deliberate resolution decisions. None of them covers quickcreate, the task 030 filter, or FR-13 ownership.

Severity: suggestion or stale comment only. It changes no behaviour, and the waiver's closing caveat (CREATE privilege is not checked; don't read this as "the route is fine") is still true. But the factual claims the reviewer quotes do contradict the merged code, so the finding stands. || I could not refute this. The claim holds, and it is not one of the seven deliberate resolution decisions.

1. **Where the text came from.** The waiver at tests/Spaarke.ArchTests/RouteAuthorizationGuardTests.cs:631-638 is our side, unchanged. It sits at HEAD:618 of that file. MERGE_HEAD has no quickcreate waiver at all (grep of the MERGE_HEAD version returns nothing), so master never wrote this text. verified.better_fix:
Keep the Permanent waiver, because Rule A cannot see the filter while FilterMarker does not credit QuickCreateSourceAccessFilter. Rewrite its text to cover four points:
(a) The route CREATES and has no target resource, but it does read a caller-named source record for field mapping, and that read is gated by `.AddQuickCreateSourceAccessFilter()` (OBO Read check that fails closed; word-add-in-r1 task 030). Rule A does not credit that filter because it is not in ExplicitlyCreditedFilterTypeNames.
(b) The write runs on the app identity. For Matter and Project the owner is load-bearing (unresolved caller → 403 owner_unresolved, no row written); only Invoice is best-effort.
(c) The caller's CREATE privilege is still not checked.
(d) Record-level Read does not apply field-level security masking (QuickCreateSourceAccessFilter.cs:59-60).
Alternatively, add "QuickCreateSourceAccessFilter" to ExplicitlyCreditedFilterTypeNames after reviewing it, which also brings it under Rule B's file discovery. Only then delete the waiver, since NoWaiverIsStale would then flag it. || Keep the Permanent waiver and rewrite its text. Don't credit QuickCreateSourceAccessFilter in FilterMarker: the filter deliberately lets requests through when they carry no source context (QuickCreateSourceAccessFilter.cs:88-94). Crediting it would tell Rule A the whole route is gated when it is only gated for requests that name a record context. It would also mean adding it to ExplicitlyCreditedFilterTypeNames, which makes Rule B inspect it. Suggested text:

"CREATE. The new record has nothing to authorize against in advance; the same reasoning as maintenance rule 2 for POST /api/v1/documents. What IS gated: when the request names a record context (SourceEntityType/SourceRecordId), QuickCreateSourceAccessFilter (word-add-in-r1 task 030) requires the caller to hold Read on it (OBO RetrievePrincipalAccess, fails closed) before RecordCreationService reads it app-only for field mapping. FilterMarker does not credit it, because it passes requests that carry no context. Owner: Matter and Project are owned by the caller and an unresolved caller is refused with 403; Invoice is still best-effort. NOT checked: whether the caller holds CREATE privilege for the entity type. The write runs on the app identity. That is a privilege question rather than a per-resource one, but a reader who takes this waiver as 'this route is fine' has read it wrong." || Keep the Permanent waiver, because Rule A still cannot see the filter, and rewrite its reason along these lines. "CREATE of a new row. The only pre-existing resource is the optional record context (SourceEntityType/SourceRecordId). QuickCreateSourceAccessFilter (word-add-in-r1 task 030) requires the caller's OBO Read right on it and fails closed; with no context it passes through, because nothing is read. Rule A does not credit it because it is not in ExplicitlyCreditedFilterTypeNames. For Matter and Project the caller is a load-bearing owner (an unresolved caller gets 403 and no row is written, per FR-13). Invoice keeps best-effort ownership. The write itself runs on the app identity, and CREATE privilege on the entity type is NOT checked. That is a privilege question outside Rule A's subject."

The other option is to add "QuickCreateSourceAccessFilter" to ExplicitlyCreditedFilterTypeNames and delete the waiver. Rule B would accept it because it consults CallerRecordAccessProbe (:1249). NoWaiverIsStale only flags Pending waivers, so if the filter is credited the waiver has to be deleted by hand; no test will force it. In the same pass, fix the stale :547-552 header, which credits /todo through the dropped AddEntityAccessFilter, and the /search/entities waiver text, which describes the dropped task-126 OBO fix.

rejected.title: The class remarks claim every endpoint authorizes via endpoint filters, which /search/entities explicitly does not
rejected.why:
This is not a merge defect, and the claim overstates what the code says.

1. The merge did not touch these lines. The class remark "All endpoints use endpoint filters for authorization per ADR-008" appears unchanged on every side: merge-base ba1a53b99 line 23, HEAD line 23, MERGE_HEAD line 29, and the merged file line 29. The /search/entities comment (merged :1013-1021) is master's task-062 text copied over as-is under deliberate decision 5. Running `git diff MERGE_HEAD` on OfficeEndpoints.cs shows only the /save-debug hunks. So master already has both the remark and the search comment side by side, and the claim itself admits "the merge did not introduce it".

2. The premise "/search/entities explicitly does not [use endpoint filters for authorization]" is wrong. The endpoint registers `.AddOfficeAuthFilter()` at merged :1028 and `.AddOfficeRateLimitFilter(...)` at :1027. The comment at :1014 opens with "Authorization: OfficeAuthFilter validates user authentication". The only thing that happens inside the query is trimming the result set row by row. The full ADR-008 allows that for list endpoints: docs/adr/ADR-008-authorization-endpoint-filters.md:66 says "List endpoints | Authorization at query construction (scoped to caller)", and :70 says the same. The class remark is a general summary. The exception is documented right at the registration it applies to, and ADR-008 sanctions it. The two do not contradict each other.

3. The AllowAnonymous routes are old and deliberate. /health (:85) is an anonymous, rate-limited health check, which CLAUDE.md §9 allows. /save-debug (:178) was AllowAnonymous at the merge-base, registers only under IsDevelopment(), and is the route whose body-logging fix (task 120) we needed to survive. It did survive: merged :132-140 logs only the length, and :172 returns bodyLength instead of bodyPreview.

At most this is slightly loose wording in an XML remark that has been in the file since before the merge. It is harmless and outside the merge's scope. || Refuted. The merge did not introduce this. It is a harmless comment-wording point, and the text in question is master's, which we kept on purpose under resolution decision #1.

1. Both passages match master exactly. The class remark at OfficeEndpoints.cs:19-33 is the same as MERGE_HEAD's (diff is empty). The /search/entities comment at :1013-1022 is the same as MERGE_HEAD:1004-1013 (diff is empty). The class remark was also present at the merge-base ba1a53b99:23 and at HEAD:23. So whatever mismatch exists is already on master; resolving the merge created none of it. The reviewer says as much.

2. The search block is decision #1 (keep master's task 062 impersonated-query fix and drop our task 126). Before the merge, our side at HEAD:798-804 said outright "There is no endpoint filter because there is no target record to authorize". That clashed with the class remark more than master's wording does. So the merge reduced the tension; it did not create it.

3. The claimed contradiction is weaker than stated. /search/entities does use endpoint filters: `.AddOfficeAuthFilter()` at :1028 and `.AddOfficeRateLimitFilter` at :1027. The comment at :1014-1021 only says that per-RECORD trimming happens inside the impersonated query. It explicitly cites ADR-008's own carve-out: "where trimming must happen inside the query, document why in the code". The same wording is recorded in projects/spaarkeai-word-add-in-r1/notes/062-entity-search-trim.md:28-29. A documented, sanctioned exception next to a general summary line is not a false premise.

4. The other exceptions are old and intended. /health `.AllowAnonymous()` at :85 dates from the merge-base, and /save-debug `.AllowAnonymous()` at :178 is registered only under `env.IsDevelopment()` (:123). The surrounding /save-debug code is our task 120 fix, which survived the merge (:132-140 log only the length; the catch at :164-173 returns `bodyLength`, not a body preview). The class remark has never counted anonymous endpoints, which does no harm.

Net: at most an old wording nicety in a doc comment, identical on master, with no behavioural or security effect. It is outside the scope of this merge. || I'm refuting this. The merge did not create the problem, and one of the claim's premises is wrong.

1. **The merge added nothing here.** `git diff MERGE_HEAD -- src/server/api/Sprk.Bff.Api/Api/Office/OfficeEndpoints.cs` shows only one difference from master: our /save-debug fix. That fix is at merged lines 132-140 (the body length is logged, never the body) and 171-172 (`bytePositionInLine`/`bodyLength` replace `bodyPreview`), and decision #5 requires it to survive. The class remark (merged :29-30, "All endpoints use endpoint filters for authorization per ADR-008") and the search comment (merged :1014-1021) are identical to master's text. On master they sit at MERGE_HEAD :29 and :1006/:1011. So the two passages already contradicted each other on origin/master. The search comment came in with master's task 062 fix, and decision #1 (owner-approved) keeps that fix. Anything in the merged file here is exactly master's state.

2. **The premise "which /search/entities explicitly does not" is wrong.** /search/entities does authorize through endpoint filters. It has `.AddOfficeAuthFilter()` at merged :1028 and `.AddOfficeRateLimitFilter(...)` at :1027. The comment at :1014-1021 does not say the route has no filter. It says the route authenticates in OfficeAuthFilter, while the per-RECORD trim of a result set happens inside the impersonated query. The class remark is loose, but it does not contradict how the route is built. Every route still uses filters and `RequireAuthorization()` on the group (:44).

3. **The AllowAnonymous routes predate the merge.** /save-debug (`.AllowAnonymous()` at :178) and /health (:85) were already AllowAnonymous at the merge-base. `git show ba1a53b99:...` shows them at :76 and :160, together with the same class remark at :23. They are not merge artifacts.

At most this is an old documentation looseness that master owns (severity "suggestion"). It is not a defect in how the merge was resolved.

trace.use_case: UC1: an internal Dataverse systemuser opens a record whose owning business unit or owning team is the same as their own business unit or one of their teams. The answer depends on which plane the request comes in on. (A) Internal plane (MDA code pages, PCF, Office add-ins with a workforce Entra token): the BFF checks the record through OBO RetrievePrincipalAccess (RPA), so Dataverse decides natively. (B) SPA/Teams workforce plane (/api/v1/external/*, the same workforce token, but broker-only with no OBO): the BFF computes access itself. It matches three columns on the record, owningbusinessunit, owningteam and ownerid, against the caller's own BU, teams and systemuserid. The match covers the three root types only: sprk_project, sprk_matter and sprk_workassignment. (C) CIAM plane: does not apply, because a CIAM caller is a contact, never a systemuser (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:322-405).
trace.identity_resolution:
Every path starts from the `oid` claim. CallerResolution.ResolveObjectId (Infrastructure/Authentication/CallerResolution.cs:89-95) accepts the short `oid` claim or the long schema-URI form. It deliberately has no fallback to `sub`/NameIdentifier; a missing oid gives 401.

INTERNAL PLANE:
(1) Document routes use AuthorizationService, then CachedAccessDataSource, then DataverseAccessDataSource.GetUserAccessAsync. That method OBO-exchanges the caller's bearer token for a Dataverse token (DataverseAccessDataSource.cs:286-297). Still under that OBO token, it runs `systemusers?$filter=azureactivedirectoryobjectid eq '{oid}'` (:307, :577-615) to get the systemuserid.
(2) Record routes use GetCallerRecordAccessAsync, then GetRecordAccessAsync. This does the OBO exchange, then the same oid lookup with an explicit per-request token (:419-430).
(3) Filters for entity, delegation, todo, quickcreate and record routes use CallerRecordAccessProbe. It does the OBO exchange and then calls WhoAmI() (CallerRecordAccessProbe.cs:357). The systemuserid comes from the credential, so the oid is never passed around as data.
(4) Office entity search (master task 062) uses CallerSystemUserResolver. It looks up oid → systemuser.azureactivedirectoryobjectid app-only (Services/Ai/Context/CallerSystemUserResolver.cs:100-106), then runs an impersonated read with MSCRMCallerID set to that systemuserid (OfficeService.cs:1821-1839).

SPA/TEAMS PLANE:
- CallerPrincipalResolver.DeterminePlane (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:293-313) picks Workforce unless `iss` contains ciamlogin.com or `tid` equals Ciam:TenantId.
- WorkforcePrincipalResolver (WorkforcePrincipalResolver.cs:99-151) calls MembershipEndpoints.ResolveSystemUserIdAsync. That is an app-only QueryExpression on systemuser.azureactivedirectoryobjectid that excludes disabled users (MembershipEndpoints.cs:398-449), cached per tenant for about 10 minutes. It returns the systemuserid.
- IdentityNormalizationService.ResolveAsync then reads two things app-only: systemuser.businessunitid, giving BusinessUnitId (IdentityNormalizationService.cs:199-224), and the teammembership rows, giving TeamIds (:665-693).

trace.mechanism_one_line: Internal plane: the BFF sends the caller's token by OBO and asks Dataverse RetrievePrincipalAccess what rights this systemuser has on this record, so Dataverse applies role depth, BU, team and share rules. SPA/Teams plane: the BFF runs an app-only FetchXml where owningbusinessunit = the caller's BU, owningteam is in the caller's teams, or ownerid = the caller, and gives a flat Read|Write|Create on every matching root.
trace.what_grants_access:
INTERNAL: Dataverse's own security model, evaluated for the resolved systemuser on the specific record by RetrievePrincipalAccess (DataverseAccessDataSource.cs:705-757 for the document or record target; CallerRecordAccessProbe.cs:406-470). A matching BU or owning team gives access only as far as Dataverse says it does:
- a role privilege at BU depth or wider, or
- owner-team membership that carries the team's roles, or
- a POA share.
The BFF never compares BU or team itself. DataverseAccessDataSource fills TeamMemberships and Roles into the snapshot (:327-331), but OperationAccessRule reads only snapshot.AccessRights (Rules/OperationAccessRule.cs:49). OperationAccessPolicy then only says which right an operation needs.

SPA/TEAMS: a structural column match in MembershipResolverService. PlatformOwnershipColumns {ownerid, owningteam, owningbusinessunit} (MembershipResolverService.cs:595-596) are admitted without any registry entry when AccessConferringOnly=true on the systemuser plane (:255-258, :688-692). BuildFetchXml then binds:
- Team descriptors → each id in identity.TeamIds (:904-909)
- BusinessUnit → identity.BusinessUnitId (:911-916)
- SystemUser → the caller's systemuserid (:864-866)
These are exact-equality OR conditions. There is no BU hierarchy, no role depth and no privilege check. AccessibleRecordSetService.ComposeForSystemUserAsync walks every page (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:997-1002) and credits each hit as a membership term (:1048-1051). Handlers then allow on CallerPrincipal.HasProjectAccess / GetEffectiveRights / GetMatterRights (e.g. ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:273, :570-571).
trace.access_level_granted:
INTERNAL: whatever RPA returns, mapped one-to-one by DataverseAccessRightsMapper (DataverseAccessRightsMapper.cs:61-71):
- Read, Write, Delete, Create, Append, AppendTo and Share are mapped.
- AssignAccess and any unknown right contribute nothing.
The operation's requirement comes from OperationAccessPolicy, for example read=Read, write=Write, download_file=Write, entity.associate_document=AppendTo, share=Share (OperationAccessPolicy.cs:139-248).

Degraded paths:
- Document path (GetUserAccessAsync): if RPA fails, it falls back to a read probe capped at Read (DataverseAccessDataSource.cs:685-687, :776-852).
- Record path (GetRecordAccessAsync): the same fallback, a probe capped at Read (:436-449).
- CallerRecordAccessProbe: no fallback; any failure gives None (CallerRecordAccessProbe.cs:446-452).

SPA/TEAMS: always the constant MembershipTermRights = Read|Write|Create (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:288-289), displayed as "Collaborate". It never includes Delete, Share, Append or AppendTo, and it ignores the user's actual Dataverse privileges. It is unioned highest-wins with any sprk_externalrecordaccess grants held by the user's linked contact (:1059-1062).

gaps_or_caveats: DESIGNED BUT NOT LIVE (ADR-028 A5 MUST is violated in code): A5 (.claude/adr/ADR-028-spaarke-auth-architecture.md:288-290) requires a workforce systemuser's root set to come from an app-only impersonated read. Live ComposeForSystemUserAsync still uses ADR-034 column matching. IImpersonatedRootSetSource is registered (ExternalAccessModule.cs:198) but nothing consumes it: the AccessibleRecordSetService constructor (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:708-713) does not take it, and the only references outside the class are static InvalidateAsync calls in InternalShareEndpoints.cs:358,473 that clear a cache nothing fills. The FR-20 flag `ExternalAccess:ImpersonatedRootSets:Enabled` appears only in tests (ImpersonationNegativeCanaryTests); no src code reads it. Stale comments still promise the swap: AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:280-282 and :994-996.

OVER-GRANT on the SPA/Teams plane: `owningbusinessunit eq <caller BU>` (MembershipResolverService.cs:911-916) matches EVERY project/matter/WA owned by anyone in the caller's BU, and gives Read|Write|Create. This happens even when the caller's role is User-depth, has no Write, or has no privilege on that entity at all. ADR-028 A5 states this defect itself ('grants BU-matched records to users whose role depth does not cover them').

UNDER-GRANT on the SPA/Teams plane: exact BU equality only, so no Parent:Child BU or Organization depth. No POA shares, which includes the creator share ProvisionProjectEndpoint writes (:726-731): a secure-project creator does not get the project on this plane through membership. No hierarchy security. Only the three root types are composed (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:519-524).

PLANE DIVERGENCE: the same user on the same record can get different answers. The internal plane is Dataverse-exact. The Teams plane is a column-match approximation with a fixed R|W|C level. The internal plane never gets Delete/Share through membership semantics, and the Teams plane never gets them at all.

FAIL-SOFT becomes a SILENT UNDER-GRANT on the Teams plane: a failed teammembership read gives empty TeamIds (IdentityNormalizationService.cs:699-706), and a failed systemuser-row read gives BusinessUnitId=null (:230-237). The degraded identity is still cached for 10 minutes (:174), so team- or BU-owned records disappear for up to 10 minutes with no error. A failed membership FetchXml throws: WalkMembershipPagesAsync does not catch (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:838-842) and neither does the strategy, so the whole request fails closed as a 500.

VETO PIPELINE applies ONLY on the SPA/Teams plane. INoAccessListReader is used only by AccessibleRecordSetService and ExternalParticipationService (grep). On that plane:
- The deny list removes even the BU/team membership term (ApplyVetoPipeline :375-378), but only if the systemuser resolves to a contact (sprk_primarycontact or email). Without one, the deny veto is skipped entirely (:608-612).
- Restricted keeps the membership term (:398-401).
- Secure suppression touches only the contact-grant term, never the membership term (:1044-1062).
On the INTERNAL plane, AuthorizationService and CallerRecordAccessProbe consult no deny list, no Restricted flag and no Secure flag; they rely solely on RPA.

SECURE RECORDS depend on an unenforced invariant. Isolation relies on ownership by the Secure Record BU's DEFAULT owner team (ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:370-379). A Dataverse BU default team automatically contains every user in that BU. So a systemuser placed in the Secure Record BU would match on BOTH planes: the Teams plane through owningbusinessunit/owningteam, and the internal plane natively. No runtime check that the BU is 'memberless' exists in src; the word appears only in comments. On the internal plane an Organization-depth role also sees secure records natively. SecureContainerDecision decides SPE container placement, not access.

DOCUMENT-SCOPED internal check: AuthorizeAsync evaluates the sprk_document row's OWN ownership (DataverseAccessDataSource.cs:373,662-663), not the parent matter's BU or team. A user whose BU matches the matter but not the document gets Dataverse's answer for the document.

RPA-under-OBO live verification is not closed (task 034 is shipped but not closed; see OperationAccessPolicy.cs:205-210). The comment that RPA already factors in teams, roles and shares (SpaarkeCore.cs:111-112) is design intent, not something this repo verified live. If RPA fails, document paths cap at Read, so every write/delete/share/download_file gate denies; CallerRecordAccessProbe denies everything.

CACHING/STALENESS: internal snapshots are cached 60s in Redis, including None results from exceptions (CachedAccessDataSource.cs:131-134, 208-210), so a transient fault becomes a 60s denial and a revoked BU/team change can still allow for up to 60s. Teams-plane caches: systemuser id about 10 min, identity 10 min, membership 5 min (MembershipResolverService.cs:112). No invalidation on BU or team reassignment was traced.

IAccessibleRecordSetService.IsRecordAccessibleAsync / IsOperationPermittedAsync (with the None-requirement guard) have no production consumers; the only consumer of the interface is WorkforcePrincipalStrategy. Enforcement is ad hoc in each handler through CallerPrincipal.HasProjectAccess / GetEffectiveRights (ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:273, :570-571). Three ComposeAsync calls run per request (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:519-524).

GetUserAccessAsync writes the OBO token onto _httpClient.DefaultRequestHeaders (DataverseAccessDataSource.cs:293). This is safe only because the typed client is transient and the data source is request-scoped, and callers run these checks sequentially (see the SemanticSearchEndpoints.cs:507 remarks). Concurrent calls within one request would race.

Office entity search (the master fix kept) relies on the go-live prerequisite prvActOnBehalfOfAnotherUser on the BFF application user. If every entity type fails, it throws (OfficeService.cs:1868-1876) instead of returning an empty picker.

MERGE RESIDUE (harmless): EntityAccessFilter.ExtractTargetEntity still contains the task-128 CreateTodoRequest branch and its remark (EntityAccessFilter.cs:329-365), but POST /api/office/todo now uses TodoSourceAccessFilter (OfficeEndpoints.cs:1536-1543), not AddEntityAccessFilter. The branch is dead code, not a hole.

Not verified here (platform behaviour): teammembership rows for Entra-group owner teams may be created only when the user first signs in to Dataverse. The Teams-plane owningteam match would then miss a group team the user has not activated yet.
trace.designed_vs_live_notes:
LIVE, internal plane: every BFF route with a per-record gate for a workforce systemuser asks Dataverse RPA under OBO. That covers DocumentAuthorizationFilter (write/delete/read/share on the document, file access, version, operations routes), FinanceAuthorizationFilter, EntityAccessFilter (Office save), TodoSourceAccessFilter (master task 064), QuickCreateSourceAccessFilter, RecordRouteAccessAuthorizationFilter, DelegationRuleFilter / InternalShareEndpoints, and the AI search / RAG / semantic-search scope=entity checks. Office entity search uses an impersonated read instead, which is still Dataverse-native. MDA forms that read Dataverse directly never touch the BFF. For UC1 on this plane the BFF holds no BU or team logic; Dataverse decides.

LIVE, SPA/Teams plane: the ADR-034 column-matching path decides. Access comes from owningbusinessunit or owningteam matching the caller, plus ownerid; platform ownership was restored structurally by task 043 C-1. The level is a fixed Read|Write|Create, followed by the veto pipeline.

DESIGNED / REGISTERED BUT INERT:
- ADR-028 A5, and the FR-20 swap (task 036) of ComposeForSystemUserAsync onto ImpersonatedRootSetSource. The source class exists and is registered, but nothing consumes it and no flag is read in production. Its own registration comment admits this (ExternalAccessModule.cs:195-196).
- The NFR-04 negative canary (task 034) exists as a test tripwire only.
Net effect: the BU over-grant and share-blind under-grant that A5 was written to remove are still live on the Teams plane.

IDataverseUserClient (now in Infrastructure/Dataverse, registered unconditionally at SpaarkeCore.cs:94-95) is not on the UC1 authorization path; it serves our task-127 communications reads.

NOT SUPPORTED: UC1 for a CIAM caller. A CIAM contact cannot be a systemuser, has no BU or team, and gets grant-only access.

Live internal-plane surfaces reached with the same workforce token run the ADR-034 column match app-only, the same as the Teams plane, and with a wider descriptor set. None of them call RPA. All three pass options null or omit AccessConferringOnly, so FilterToAccessConferringRoles is skipped. Every discovered descriptor then confers: owningbusinessunit, owningteam and ownerid, plus maker-authored systemuser, team, BU, account and contact lookups. Separately, the workspace portfolio filters app-only by ownerid alone, so team-owned and BU-owned matters never appear there.

trace.identity_resolution:
1) Plane selection: CallerPrincipalResolver.DeterminePlane (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:293-313) picks CIAM only when iss contains 'ciamlogin.com' or tid equals Ciam:TenantId. Every other token is Workforce. The default JwtBearer scheme is a single tenant (AzureAd:TenantId, appsettings.template.json:38), so only home-tenant tokens get here, and B2B guests of that tenant are included.
2) oid claim: CallerResolution.ResolveObjectId reads 'oid' or the objectidentifier schema claim (CallerResolution.cs:89-95). A missing or non-GUID oid returns 401 missing_identity_claims (WorkforcePrincipalResolver.cs:99-108). The MembershipEndpoints doc comment that also claims a NameIdentifier fallback is stale.
3) systemuser branch, which UC2 skips: MembershipEndpoints.ResolveSystemUserIdAsync queries systemuser where azureactivedirectoryobjectid = oid AND isdisabled = false (MembershipEndpoints.cs:434-457), with a 10-minute oid-to-systemuserid cache (MembershipEndpoints.cs:409-420, TTL at :86). No row, or a DISABLED row, sends the caller to the contact branch. A user disabled within the last 10 minutes can still be served from the cache as a systemuser.
4) Contact branch: IIdentityNormalizationService.TryResolveContactByWorkforceIdentityAsync (IdentityNormalizationService.cs:242-303).
  (a) contact.azureactivedirectoryobjectid = oid, TopCount 1 (IdentityNormalizationService.cs:535-577). On a fault this returns null and falls through to (b).
  (b) Fallback: contact.emailaddress1 = the verified-email claim. The claim order is email, then preferred_username, then upn, then ClaimTypes.Email (WorkforcePrincipalResolver.cs:220-228). The query is TopCount 2 (IdentityNormalizationService.cs:590-654). The pure DecideWorkforceEmailMatch (:482-531) returns a deny for more than one match, for a contact already bound to a different oid (the A-18 no-hijack rule), for an unreadable binding, or for an empty caller oid. Otherwise it resolves.
  (c) If neither matches, or resolution throws, the result is 403 sdap.access.deny.principal_not_resolved (WorkforcePrincipalResolver.cs:162-212).
The resolved value is WorkforcePrincipal{Kind=ContactOnly, ContactId, SystemUserId=null} (ExternalCallerContext.cs:444-452). WorkforcePrincipalStrategy then turns it into CallerPrincipal{Plane=Workforce, ContactId, SystemUserId=null} (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:537-547). Nothing on this plane ever writes an oid binding (IdentityNormalizationService.cs:478-480), so an email-resolved contact re-resolves by email on every request.
trace.mechanism_one_line: Workforce JWT, then the ExternalCollaboration dual-scheme policy and the group CallerPrincipalAuthorizationFilter. The resolver picks the Workforce plane by issuer and finds no enabled systemuser for the oid, then maps the caller to a contact by contact.azureactivedirectoryobjectid, else by email claim with the no-hijack check. AccessibleRecordSetService.ComposeForContactAsync then builds an app-only (rootId -> AccessRights) map for project, matter and work assignment: sprk_externalrecordaccess grants (direct plus org-inherited) ∪ standing-grant membership ∪ org-expansion membership, with Secure pre-max suppression, then the deny-list veto, then the Restricted veto. Handlers gate on KEY PRESENCE for most reads and on rights flags for to-do lists and writes, and data and bytes are served app-only. Dataverse row security is never consulted, because a contact is not a security principal.
trace.what_grants_access:
All reads are app-only against Dataverse and run inside ComposeForContactAsync (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:1114-1322). Four sources can add a record; two vetoes can remove it.

Additive terms (combined highest-wins by bitwise OR in AccumulateTerm, :308-318):
- (T1) The contact's own active, unexpired sprk_externalrecordaccess grant rows: _sprk_contact_value = contact, statecode 0, sprk_expiresdate >= today. A null expiry confers nothing (ExternalParticipationService.cs:61-62, 108-109).
- (T1b) ORGANIZATION grant rows (contact empty) for every sprk_organization the contact is an ACTIVE member of in the sprk_contactorganization junction (:909-942, 1020-1060, 1096-1132). Both T1 and T1b come from GetGrantSetAsync, which is Redis-cached for 60 seconds (:189-227). They cover project, matter and work-assignment roots only (:1128-1132).
- (T2) Standing-grant membership. It applies ONLY if contact.sprk_standinggrant = true AND sprk_accesspermissiongrant is set. That field is FLS-secured, and the read fails closed to NotHeld (SubjectStandingGrantReader.cs:155-237). Records come from MembershipResolverService.ResolveByContactAsync: contact-typed lookups in the access-conferring registry only, with platform ownership excluded (MembershipResolverService.cs:384-539, 614-700). They are credited at the contact's baseline (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:1158-1175, 1270-1277).
- (T3) Org expansion. For each active org whose own standing grant and baseline are set, records that reference that org through registry-listed org-typed lookups are credited at the org's baseline, one walk per distinct baseline (:1195-1249, 1283-1290).
- There is NO automatic contact-anchored membership without a standing grant (:1139-1141, 1161).

Secure (sprk_issecure) suppression, applied before the max:
- T2 and T3 are dropped outright on secure roots.
- T1/T1b contribute only DirectAccessLevel, so org-inherited rows contribute None (:237-259, 1262-1265).

Vetoes, applied after the max (:357-407, 1298-1301):
- The deny list (sprk_noaccessentry) for the contact and its active orgs (:596-672) removes keys.
- Restricted (sprk_accesspermission = 100000002) removes EVERY key for a contact principal, because the survivor map is empty (:1301). So a UC2 user can never reach a Restricted root.

Children and other modules:
- Children are reached only through an accessible root: documents, invoices and to-dos (ExternalAccessModule.cs:244-268).
- Service requests are visible only where sprk_requestedby = the caller's contactId (:299-308).
- Grid configuration is a static allow-list (:318-324).
trace.access_level_granted:
Each record's rights are the OR of its terms. The mapping is ExternalAccessLevels.ToAccessRights (ExternalCallerContext.cs:207-213): ViewOnly = Read; Collaborate = Read|Create|Write; FullAccess = Read|Create|Write|Delete; null or out-of-range = None. The standing and org baselines use the same mapping (SubjectStandingGrantReader.cs:61).

How the endpoints enforce it:
- Most reads check KEY PRESENCE only, not Read: GET /projects, /projects/{id}, /documents, document content download, /versions, /events, /contacts, /organizations, and module /fetch and /record. They use HasProjectAccess (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:161) or the id sets (ExternalModuleRegistry.cs:129-144).
- To-do lists require Read (ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:399-401).
- POST to-dos, events and document upload require Create (:433-434, :797-798, :570-571).
- PATCH /todos/{id} requires Write (:903).
- No route consumes Delete on this plane.

So a record can sit in the set with AccessRights.None, and it is still readable wherever the check is presence-only.

gaps_or_caveats: LIKELY DEFECT — Secure suppression does not stop reads. It removes RIGHTS but not VISIBILITY. On a secure root reached only by an ORG-inherited grant, the grant term contributes DirectAccessLevel=null, which maps to None, and the id stays in the map (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:232-234, 1262-1265). WorkforcePrincipalStrategy copies None-rights keys into ProjectAccess, MatterAccess and WorkAssignmentAccess (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:527-529, 545-546). HasProjectAccess is presence-only (:161), and so are the module scopes (ExternalAccessModule.cs:250-291). So GET /projects/{id}, /documents, the document content DOWNLOAD, /versions, /events, /contacts, /organizations and module /fetch and /record all succeed on that secure record. Only to-do lists (Read), creates (Create) and PATCH (Write) deny. This contradicts the ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:31-34 header ('READ routes verify the caller holds Read'). Found by reading the code; not reproduced by a test.

LIKELY DEFECT — the grant cache drops the provenance field. CachedParticipation and CachedRootGrant store only AccessLevel (ExternalParticipationService.cs:1242-1268), so on a cache hit (:208) DirectAccessLevel is null for EVERY grant. Within each 60-second TTL window, a DIRECT ViewOnly/Collaborate/FullAccess grant on a SECURE root collapses to None. The caller then gets intermittent 403s on to-do list, create and PATCH, while presence-gated reads still pass. This is the reverse of the cache-shape bug the task-032 comment describes; CacheVersion (4) was not bumped for the task-037 field.

Email-fallback trust. An UNBOUND contact (azureactivedirectoryobjectid empty) resolves to any workforce-tenant caller whose email/preferred_username/upn claim equals contact.emailaddress1 (IdentityNormalizationService.cs:467-472, 482-531). The no-hijack check protects only contacts already bound to a different oid. If the binding column is missing or unpopulated in an environment, the guard is inert and only logs a WARNING (:620-635). Nothing on this plane ever writes the binding (:478-480). B2B guests in the workforce tenant take the same path; the plane cannot tell employees from guests.

Branch selection is by systemuser row state. A systemuser with isdisabled=true, which is typical for a license-removed user, is treated as NOT a systemuser and drops into the contact branch (MembershipEndpoints.cs:448-451). Conversely, the 10-minute oid-to-systemuserid cache (MembershipEndpoints.cs:409-420, :86) keeps a just-disabled user on the systemuser path. An unlicensed user who still has an ENABLED systemuser row is NOT on this UC2 path at all.

Fail directions differ by source:
- Grant query fault: ExternalGrantSet.Empty, and that empty result is CACHED for 60s — a silent under-grant (ExternalParticipationService.cs:857-862, 989-993, 218-224).
- Org-grant or junction fault: an empty list, so nothing additive is contributed, BUT the deny wall's ORG axis also silently stops matching; contact-keyed deny rows still apply (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:578-589).
- Flag read fault: secure+restricted, so the contact loses the record (fail-closed).
- Deny-list or org-reference fault: every candidate is denied.
- Standing read fault: NotHeld.
- Membership-walk or systemuser-lookup exception: propagates unhandled, giving a 500 rather than an audited deny (MembershipResolverService.cs:507-509; MembershipEndpoints.cs:453).
- Contact-resolution exception: 403 deny.

Restricted roots are STRUCTURALLY unreachable for UC2: the veto's survivor map is empty for contact principals (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:1301). Access is also limited to three root types plus their children. Documents under matters or work assignments can be listed through the documents module, but the content-download and versions routes are project-only (document->project check, ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:333-341, 702-710), so those bytes cannot be downloaded through them.

Standing membership is NOT automatic. A contact without sprk_standinggrant=true AND a populated sprk_accesspermissiongrant gets explicit grants only. contact.sprk_standinggrant is FLS-secured, so if the BFF app user lacks the FSP the whole term goes dark with only a WARNING (SubjectStandingGrantReader.cs:177-185).

Tier-1 module entitlement is not enforced on the data routes. /api/dataverse/fetch and /record check only registry.FindByEntity (ExternalModuleDataEndpoints.cs:156-164, 261-265). ModuleEntitlementResolver output is advisory (MeEntitlementsEndpoint.cs:21-22). A UC2 caller with no App-Role can still call any registered module directly, bounded only by Tier-2 record scope. This contradicts ADR-028 A3 (:118, :124).
The Capped (NFR-03) flag is computed on AccessibleRecordSet but is not carried onto CallerPrincipal (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:537-547). A 5,000-row-capped set is therefore presented as complete.

Grant DATA is cached for 60s (authorization decisions are not cached). A revocation or expiry can take up to 60s to bite unless the writer invalidates the cache (ExternalParticipationService.cs:18, 252-284).

Cross-plane inconsistency: if the same contact authenticates on the CIAM plane, CiamContactPrincipalStrategy applies NO Secure suppression, NO deny list and NO Restricted veto (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:378-404). The same person can therefore see more through CIAM than through the workforce plane.

NOT SUPPORTED on internal surfaces (MDA, Office, /api/* routes using AuthorizationService or OBO), because those require a Dataverse systemuser: DataverseAccessDataSource denies with 'caller_not_a_dataverse_user' (DataverseAccessDataSource.cs:426-430, 307-320). The /api/v1/external-access management routes are also denied: the DelegationRuleFilter probe's WhoAmI resolves no systemuser (CallerRecordAccessProbe.cs:230-234). A UC2 user can never grant, share or manage access.

- ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:31-34 claims READ routes verify Read; only the to-do lists do.

ADR-028 versus the live code:
- A2 (:73) reads as if a non-systemuser automatically gets contact-anchored membership. In the live code, membership applies only when a standing grant with a baseline exists (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:1161).
- A3 (:118, :124) requires server-enforced Tier-1 module entitlement; it is not enforced (see gaps).
- A1/A2/A3 broker-only IS honoured on this path. There is no OBO: the identity lookups, grants, flags, membership walks, data reads, SPE download and upload are all app-only (ExternalParticipationService.cs:1170-1194; ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:343-349).

corrections.claim: gaps_or_caveats (Email-fallback trust): 'If the binding column is missing or unpopulated in an environment, the guard is inert and only logs a WARNING (:620-635).'
corrections.problem: This treats a missing column and an empty column as the same case, and they behave in opposite ways. The email-fallback query puts azureactivedirectoryobjectid in its ColumnSet. In an environment where contact.azureactivedirectoryobjectid does not exist, Dataverse rejects a query that names an unknown attribute, so the query throws. The catch returns null, and the caller treats null as a deny (contact_binding_unreadable). The oid-first lookup filters on the same column, so it also faults and returns null. In such an environment, every UC2 caller gets 403 principal_not_resolved. The whole UC2 path fails closed there; it is not an inert guard. The 'inert + WARNING' path only runs when the column exists but is null on every matched row. The code comment at :620-626 ('missing or universally empty') makes the same mistake.
corrections.correction: Split the caveat. (1) Column present but unpopulated: the no-hijack guard is inert, only a WARNING is logged, and any workforce caller whose email claim matches resolves to the unbound contact. (2) Column not provisioned: both lookups fault, and every non-systemuser workforce caller is denied. UC2 is then unusable, not over-permissive, in that environment. Repo notes say the column may be absent in spaarkedev1, so whether UC2 is live at all depends on the environment's schema.
corrections.evidence: IdentityNormalizationService.cs:596-605 (ColumnSet("contactid","azureactivedirectoryobjectid")); :646-653 (catch returns null); :273-282 (null means DENIED with DenyContactBindingUnreadable); :547-550 and :568-575 (the oid lookup filters on the same column and returns null on a fault); :144-145 and :211-212 ('environments that provision that field', 'isn't provisioned in every environment'); projects/spaarke-ai-platform-unification-r7/notes/audits/wave12-120-assistant-workspace.md:434 ('contact.azureactivedirectoryobjectid field appears not to be present in the spaarkedev1 schema'). The runtime Dataverse behaviour was inferred, not reproduced.

corrections.claim: identity_resolution 4(b): 'The claim order is email, then preferred_username, then upn, then ClaimTypes.Email (WorkforcePrincipalResolver.cs:220-228).'
corrections.problem: That is the order the source code lists, not the order that actually runs. The BFF keeps inbound claim-type mapping ON, which renames the token's short 'email' claim to ClaimTypes.Email and 'upn' to ClaimTypes.Upn. So FindFirst("email") and FindFirst("upn") never match. The effective order is preferred_username first, then the mapped ClaimTypes.Email. This matters for security: preferred_username is the mutable UPN, and it wins over the email claim when the caller is matched to contact.emailaddress1.
corrections.correction: State the effective order: preferred_username, then ClaimTypes.Email (the mapped 'email'). The short-name 'email' and 'upn' lookups are dead under mapping.
corrections.evidence: WorkforcePrincipalResolver.cs:222-225; CallerResolution.cs:22-24 ('With inbound claim-type mapping left on — the default, and what this app runs — .NET renames the token's claims') and :37-41 ('short "oid" DOESN'T EXIST under mapping'); AuthorizationModule.cs:49 (AddMicrosoftIdentityWebApi, with no MapInboundClaims override; a grep for MapInboundClaims finds nothing).

corrections.claim: what_grants_access (vetoes): 'Restricted (sprk_accesspermission = 100000002) removes EVERY key for a contact principal, because the survivor map is empty (:1301).'
corrections.problem: Read literally, this is wrong. The Restricted slot only removes keys whose root is flagged IsRestricted. That includes roots whose flag read failed, because unreadable flags are treated as secure AND restricted. Non-restricted keys are kept. The empty survivor map only means that no contact-sourced restricted key survives.
corrections.correction: The Restricted veto removes every key whose root is flagged Restricted, or whose flags could not be read. On the contact plane none of those survive, because the survivor map is empty. Other keys are unaffected.
corrections.evidence: AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:391-406 (`if (!flags.TryGetValue(recordId, out var f) || !f.IsRestricted) continue;`); :1301 (EmptyRights survivor map); ExternalParticipationService.cs:589-592 and :603-608 (unreadable or unreturned flags become Unreadable).

corrections.claim: gaps_or_caveats (grant cache): 'Within each 60-second TTL window, a DIRECT ViewOnly/Collaborate/FullAccess grant on a SECURE root collapses to None. The caller then gets intermittent 403s...'
corrections.problem: The defect is real, but 'intermittent' understates it. Only a cache miss carries DirectAccessLevel. Every request after the first in each 60-second window reads the cached shape, which has no DirectAccessLevel. WorkforcePrincipalStrategy also calls ComposeAsync three times per request (project, matter, work assignment), and each call reads GetGrantSetAsync. So the matter and work-assignment compositions in the cache-missing request can already hit the fire-and-forget cache write. Direct grants on secure roots therefore read as None on most requests, not occasionally. The CacheVersion point is also secondary: the cached shape never gained the field at all.
corrections.correction: On the workforce plane, direct grants on secure roots come out as None on nearly every request while the Redis cache is warm. Only the first composition after a miss sees the direct level. The fix is to add DirectAccessLevel to CachedParticipation and CachedRootGrant and bump CacheVersion, not only the bump.
corrections.evidence: ExternalParticipationService.cs:201-209 (cache hit returns cached.ToGrantSet()); :223 (fire-and-forget CacheGrantSetAsync); :1141-1153 (only AccessLevel is persisted); :1242-1268 (ToParticipation and ToGrant never set DirectAccessLevel); CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:519-524 (three sequential ComposeAsync calls); AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:1130, :244, :250, :256 (secure roots use DirectAccessLevel).

corrections.claim: identity_resolution 1: 'The default JwtBearer scheme is a single tenant (AzureAd:TenantId, appsettings.template.json:38), so only home-tenant tokens get here, and B2B guests of that tenant are included.'
corrections.problem: The repo code does not verify this. AuthorizationModule only calls AddMicrosoftIdentityWebApi(AzureAd). It sets no ValidIssuers and no IssuerValidator, and nothing checks tid against AzureAd:TenantId. Whether tokens from other tenants validate depends on Microsoft.Identity.Web's issuer validator and on the app registration's sign-in audience, not on code here. ADR-028 A2 mandates a MULTITENANT registration for the Teams host. If tokens from a foreign tenant are accepted, DeterminePlane sends them to the Workforce plane, and the email fallback would let a user from another tenant resolve to an unbound contact.
corrections.correction: Mark tenant restriction as a library/configuration property that the repo does not enforce. State that ADR-028 A2 intends multitenant sign-in. Note that, if cross-tenant tokens validate, the email-fallback caveat extends beyond B2B guests to users of any tenant.
corrections.evidence: AuthorizationModule.cs:47-49 (AddMicrosoftIdentityWebApi only); a Grep for IssuerValidator|ValidIssuers in Sprk.Bff.Api finds only the Ciam scheme's ValidateIssuer=true (:67); CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:293-313 (anything not CIAM is Workforce); .claude/adr/ADR-028-spaarke-auth-architecture.md:70 ('against a **multitenant** app registration (per-customer admin consent)'). The library's runtime behaviour was not verified.

corrections.claim: identity_resolution 4 / mechanism: the contact is resolved by contact.azureactivedirectoryobjectid, else by email (with no mention of contact state).
corrections.problem: This omits a material caveat. Neither the oid lookup nor the email lookup filters contact.statecode, so a DEACTIVATED contact still resolves as a UC2 principal. Its still-active sprk_externalrecordaccess rows still confer access, because the grant filter checks the grant row's statecode, not the contact's. An inactive duplicate contact with the same email also makes the active one ambiguous, which causes a deny. The contact-only branch also never consults systemuser.sprk_primarycontact, which the code calls the authoritative systemuser-to-contact link. A disabled systemuser whose contact is linked only that way is therefore found only by email.
corrections.correction: Add these caveats: deactivating a contact does not revoke workforce-plane access, and an inactive duplicate contact with the same email causes an ambiguity deny. For a disabled systemuser, the contact is found by contact.azureactivedirectoryobjectid or by email only, never through sprk_primarycontact.
corrections.evidence: IdentityNormalizationService.cs:541-550 (oid query: one condition, no statecode); :596-605 (email query: one condition, no statecode); :496-499 (more than one match means DenyAmbiguousEmail); ExternalParticipationService.cs:61-62 (grant filter on the grant's own statecode only); IdentityNormalizationService.cs:140-146 and :209-212 (sprk_primarycontact is authoritative, used only on the systemuser branch); WorkforcePrincipalResolver.cs:160-167.

corrections.claim: gaps_or_caveats: 'Grant DATA is cached for 60s ... A revocation or expiry can take up to 60s to bite' (presented as the only data-staleness window).
corrections.problem: This omits the longer cache. The standing-grant (T2) and org-expansion (T3) membership walks go through MembershipResolverService.ResolveByContactAsync, which caches the resolved membership response for 5 minutes. Removing a contact from a registry-listed assignment lookup, or an org reference from a record, can therefore keep the derived access for up to 5 minutes. The standing flags themselves are read live. No invalidation hook is described for this cache.
corrections.correction: State the two data-cache windows: 60 seconds for grant rows (T1/T1b) and 5 minutes for membership results (T2/T3).
corrections.evidence: MembershipResolverService.cs:112 (CacheTtl = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5)); :437-446 (contact-path cache lookup); :529 (TrySetCacheAsync on the resolved response); AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:1165-1169 and :1237-1243 (T2/T3 walks call ResolveByContactAsync).

corrections.claim: what_grants_access (T1b / T3): 'ORGANIZATION grant rows ... for every sprk_organization the contact is an ACTIVE member of in the sprk_contactorganization junction' / 'For each active org whose own standing grant and baseline are set'.
corrections.problem: 'Active' is overstated. Membership is bounded only by the junction row's statecode, deliberately not by sprk_enddate, so an ended-but-not-deactivated membership still confers access. The organization's own state is never checked: the org-grant rows, the junction row and the org standing read don't look at sprk_organization.statecode, and the 'org' in 'active org' is not checked either. The reconciliation job that would deactivate ended memberships and grants of inactive organizations is registered enabled:false and is report-only. The T1b org-grant membership is also read separately inside the 60-second-cached grant set. The T3 term and the deny-veto subject use a different, live junction read. So T1b and the org axis of the ethical wall can come from different snapshots.
corrections.correction: Say 'membership rows with statecode=0 (end date not enforced; organization status not checked; reconciliation job ships disabled)'. Note that the T1b membership snapshot can be up to 60 seconds stale relative to the veto's organization subject.
corrections.evidence: AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:478-483 ('The query bounds on statecode only; it does NOT bound on sprk_enddate'); ExternalParticipationService.cs:1101-1103 (junction filter: _sprk_contact_value and statecode eq 0 only); :68-72 (org grant filter: no org status); :914 (org-grant rows read inside the cached QueryGrantSetAsync); AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:1137 (separate live ReadActiveOrgMembershipsAsync); ExternalAccessModule.cs:355-372 (ExternalAccessReconciliationJob registered with enabled: false, writes report-only).

corrections.claim: gaps_or_caveats: 'NOT SUPPORTED on internal surfaces (MDA, Office, /api/* routes using AuthorizationService or OBO), because those require a Dataverse systemuser' / summary: 'Those need OBO plus RetrievePrincipalAccess or WhoAmI'.
corrections.problem: The conclusion (deny) holds for the routes checked, but the stated mechanism is not universal. After the merge, /api/office/search/entities keys on MSCRMCallerID impersonation through CallerSystemUserResolver (master's task 062), not OBO. The internal /api/dataverse/* passthrough group gates on UserPrivilegeChecker's oid-to-systemuser mapping, not RetrievePrincipalAccess or WhoAmI. Both fail closed for a non-systemuser for a different reason than stated. The claim that no internal route is reachable was not shown exhaustively: the trace sampled only DataverseAccessDataSource and CallerRecordAccessProbe.
corrections.correction: Say that the internal routes checked all key on an oid-to-systemuser mapping (OBO+RPA, OBO+WhoAmI, MSCRMCallerID impersonation, or a role-privilege lookup), and each fails closed without one. Keep 'structurally cannot' scoped to the routes verified.
corrections.evidence: Services/Ai/Context/CallerSystemUserResolver.cs:106 (systemuser lookup by oid); Services/Dataverse/Privileges/UserPrivilegeChecker.cs:133-140 ('Could not map Azure AD oid ... failing closed'); Api/Dataverse/RecordEndpoints.cs:40-48 (RequireAuthorization + AddDataverseAuthorizationFilter); DataverseAccessDataSource.cs:426-430; CallerRecordAccessProbe.cs:224-234 (the deny can occur at the OBO exchange, :227-228, or at WhoAmI, :230-234).

corrections.claim: gaps_or_caveats: 'Cross-plane inconsistency: ... The same person can therefore see more through CIAM than through the workforce plane.'
corrections.problem: This is only half the asymmetry. CIAM does skip Secure suppression, the deny list and the Restricted veto. But CIAM is grants-only: it gets no standing-grant (T2) and no org-expansion (T3) membership. A contact with a standing grant can therefore reach records on the workforce plane that it cannot reach on CIAM.
corrections.correction: The planes diverge in both directions. CIAM over-exposes secure, restricted and walled roots reached by grants. The workforce plane additionally grants standing and org-expansion membership, which CIAM never applies.
corrections.evidence: CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:375-404 (CIAM: GetGrantSetAsync only, with the comment 'No membership/assignment/rollup-derived access for a CIAM partner'); AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:1158-1175 and :1195-1249 (workforce T2/T3).

trace.use_case: UC3: An external contact (CIAM / Entra External ID, e.g. outside counsel) accesses a record through the external SPA. The CIAM token only authenticates on /api/v1/external/*. The caller reaches roots (project, matter, work assignment) and their children (documents, invoices, to-dos, events). All data is read and written app-only by the BFF.
trace.identity_resolution:
Token: the "Ciam" JwtBearer scheme (AuthorizationModule.cs:59-71) validates issuer, audience, lifetime and signing key against {Ciam:Instance}/{Ciam:TenantId}/v2.0. Only the ExternalCollaboration policy (AuthorizationModule.cs:351-359) admits that scheme, and only the /api/v1/external group uses the policy (ExternalAccessEndpoints.cs:54-57). The CiamExternal policy (AuthorizationModule.cs:339-343) is defined but never applied. No DefaultPolicy or FallbackPolicy override exists, so a CIAM token gets 401 on every other route.

Plane: CallerPrincipalResolver.DeterminePlane (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:293-313) picks CiamContact when the `iss` claim contains "ciamlogin.com" or `tid` equals Ciam:TenantId.

Claim to row: CiamContactPrincipalStrategy (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:345-373) reads `oid` (or the objectidentifier URI), plus preferred_username, upn or email as a fallback. ExternalParticipationService.ResolveExternalContactAsync (ExternalParticipationService.cs:314-361) resolves the Contact:
- Step 1: an app-only query `contacts?$filter=sprk_externalobjectid eq '{oid}'` (ExternalParticipationService.cs:366-398). A hit is authoritative.
- Step 2 (first-login fallback): `emailaddress1 eq '{email}'` (ExternalParticipationService.cs:414-453). This succeeds only if the contact is unbound (the oid is then bound via PATCH If-Match:*, lines 460-493) or already bound to the same oid. A contact bound to a different oid is denied (no email hijack).
- Normally the oid is written earlier, at invite time (InviteExternalUserEndpoint.cs:140-144).

Deny outcomes: no oid and no email gives 401. An unresolved contact gives 403 `sdap.access.deny.contact_not_found`.

Result: a CallerPrincipal with Plane=CiamContact, ContactId set and SystemUserId=null (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:390-404). It is stored on HttpContext.Items by CallerPrincipalAuthorizationFilter.cs:32-49 and re-resolved on every request. The CIAM contact is never a Dataverse principal: no systemuser, no OBO, no impersonation.
trace.mechanism_one_line: CIAM token → oid → Contact (sprk_externalobjectid) → app-only read of the contact's active, unexpired sprk_externalrecordaccess rows, direct plus inherited from their organization, highest level wins → the per-root (id → AccessRights) maps on CallerPrincipal → BFF route gates (HasProjectAccess / Read / Create / Write flags) and module Tier-2 id-set filters → app-only Dataverse and SPE I/O. The UAC evaluator and its veto pipeline (deny-list, Restricted, Secure) are NOT run on this plane.
trace.what_grants_access:
Only explicit sprk_externalrecordaccess grant rows, read app-only (ExternalParticipationService.QueryGrantSetAsync, ExternalParticipationService.cs:832-994).

Term 1, the contact's own rows: `_sprk_contact_value eq {contactId} and statecode eq 0 and sprk_expiresdate ge {today}` (lines 61-62 and 108-109). A null expiry confers nothing (ISS-009 / D-1).

Term 3, organization grants: rows with an empty contact, for any org the contact is an active member of via sprk_contactorganization with statecode 0 (lines 914-942, 1020-1060, 1096-1132).

Each row targets exactly one root through a typed lookup: sprk_project, sprk_matter or sprk_workassignment. Invoice-level grants are deliberately not read. Duplicates are merged highest-wins (lines 953-976).

Who can create a grant: POST /api/v1/external-access/grant and /invite-and-grant, on the workforce admin group. DelegationRuleFilter requires the internal granter to hold Write on the target record, checked via an OBO RetrievePrincipalAccess probe (DelegationRuleFilter.cs:155-179). The grant is an upsert with a mandatory expiry that defaults to today + DefaultExpiryDays (GrantExternalAccessEndpoint.cs:186-383).

What does NOT grant CIAM access:
- Dataverse security roles, BU, owner team, POA shares or Secure-Record provisioning. The contact is not a Dataverse principal.
- The standing grant (contact.sprk_standinggrant) and org-expansion (FR-24/25). Both exist only in AccessibleRecordSetService.ComposeForContactAsync, which serves workforce contact-only principals.
- Tier-1 module entitlements. The CIAM set is blanket "assigned-work" (ModuleEntitlementResolver.cs:94-97) and only /me/entitlements consumes it, for the UI (MeEntitlementsEndpoint.cs:28). No data route enforces it.
trace.access_level_granted:
Per root, from the grant row's sprk_accesslevel via the single mapping at ExternalCallerContext.cs:207-213. Highest wins across direct and org-inherited rows:
- ViewOnly (100000000) → Read
- Collaborate (100000001) → Read | Create | Write
- FullAccess (100000002) → Read | Create | Write | Delete
- null or unknown → None

No external route deletes anything, so in practice FullAccess behaves exactly like Collaborate.

Project rows without a level are dropped (ExternalParticipationService.cs:872, 921). Matter and work-assignment rows keep a null level and resolve to None (lines 890-907).

Projects map into CallerPrincipal.ProjectAccess; matters and work assignments into MatterAccess and WorkAssignmentAccess (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:386-403, 417-429).

What each right unlocks:
- Project routes gate on membership (HasProjectAccess): read, documents list, download and versions, events, contacts, organizations (ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:273, 290, 322, 694, 766, 823, 840).
- To-do list needs Read on the root (lines 399-401). To-do create needs Create (433-434). To-do PATCH needs Write on the to-do's resolved root (897-903). These go through RightsForRoot (467-474) and cover all three root types.
- Document upload and event create need Create, projects only (570-571, 797-798).
- Module reads (/api/v1/external/api/dataverse/fetch and /record) filter by id-set membership only, not by rights (ExternalModuleDataEndpoints.cs:181-209, 268-274). The id sets come from the descriptors at ExternalAccessModule.cs:224-292: projects; documents via any accessible project, matter or WA; invoices via matter or project; WA own id; matter own id. Service requests are always empty for CIAM (lines 299-308).

gaps_or_caveats: VETO PIPELINE DOES NOT APPLY TO CIAM (confirmed). CiamContactPrincipalStrategy builds rights directly from the grant set (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:378-404) and never calls AccessibleRecordSetService, whose ComposeAsync accepts only WorkforcePrincipal (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:728-746). Only that service and ExternalParticipationService read sprk_accesspermission, GetRootRecordFlagsAsync or INoAccessListReader. Effect: FR-21 Restricted, FR-22 Secure suppression and FR-23 deny-list / ethical wall are never evaluated for an outside-counsel contact. Spec FR-21's own acceptance case ('a contact with an explicit Full Access grant is denied on a Restricted record', projects/unified-access-control-r2/spec.md:84) is violated on this plane, and FR-19 says the evaluator serves 'every principal kind' (spec.md:82). The grant endpoints have no write-side guard either: no Restricted, IsSecure or NoAccess checks in Grant*/InviteAndGrant*.

SECURE (sprk_issecure) DOES NOTHING FOR CIAM. The CIAM strategy uses AccessLevel, the effective level across all sources (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:386-388, 423), not DirectAccessLevel. So an ORGANIZATION grant held by the contact's firm confers access to a secure project, matter or WA, which FR-22 says must be suppressed. Secure provisioning (Secure Record BU, memberless owner team, POA shares) only affects internal Dataverse principals. The one CIAM-visible effect is that uploads go to the record's own container or fail with 422 (ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:598-617).

STANDING GRANT and ORG-EXPANSION (FR-24/25) are NOT applied to CIAM. They live only in AccessibleRecordSetService.ComposeForContactAsync, the workforce contact-only path. This is still open as design-register C-2 (notes/design-register.md:96).

PLAUSIBLE, not observed live: ≤60s grant/revoke latency with invalidation that misses. The CIAM read caches under the CIAM token's tid (ExternalParticipationService.cs:193-202, 290-296). Grant and revoke invalidate under the ADMIN's workforce tid (GrantExternalAccessEndpoint.cs:500, 513-514; RevokeExternalAccessEndpoint.cs:197-208). Cache keys include the tenant (TenantCache.cs:257-258), so the explicit invalidation never hits the CIAM entry. Revocation takes effect only at TTL expiry. This assumes the CIAM token carries tid; if it does not, caching is skipped entirely (lines 197 and 221).

Grant-read failure fails closed but sticks. A failed Dataverse query returns ExternalGrantSet.Empty (ExternalParticipationService.cs:856-862, 989-993), and GetGrantSetAsync still caches it for 60s (lines 221-224). The caller sees 200 with an empty list on /projects and /me for up to a minute, not an error (ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:256-258). The CIAM strategy never denies on an empty grant set.

Membership gates vs rights gates. Project read, download and events routes check HasProjectAccess (membership), not the Read flag. For CIAM this equals Read, because project rows without a level are dropped (ExternalParticipationService.cs:872, 921). Matter and WA rows with a null level are KEPT with None rights (lines 890-907). The module seam gates on id-set membership (ExternalModuleDataEndpoints.cs:268; ExternalModuleRegistry.cs:129-144), so such a grant would confer READ through /api/dataverse fetch and record (including child documents and invoices) while the to-do routes deny it (Read check). Latent: the code comment says every dev grant row has a level.

NOT SUPPORTED (structural): content download for documents parented only to a matter or work assignment. The documents module lists them via matter/WA scope dimensions (ExternalAccessModule.cs:244-254). But the only content and versions routes are /projects/{id}/documents/{docId}/..., which require the document's _sprk_project_value to equal the route id plus project access (ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:322-341, 694-710). Upload, events, contacts and organizations are also project-only.
FullAccess's Delete right is never used: no MapDelete exists on /api/v1/external, so FullAccess and Collaborate behave the same.
Tier-1 module entitlements are advisory. /me/entitlements is the only consumer, and no data route checks entitlement. Every registered module is reachable subject only to Tier-2 id sets.

Column exposure on the module seam is not narrowed. Reads run app-only with the full privilege of the BFF's app identity: the caller-chosen $select at RecordService.cs:68-74 and caller FetchXML attributes. Dataverse row, column and FLS security for a human principal is never consulted. The RecordService.cs:22-26 remark about 'impersonated CallerId' is stale for this path: no CallerId is set on IDataverseService.

Contact resolution has no statecode filter (ExternalParticipationService.cs:375, 423). Deactivating the Dataverse contact does not revoke access; the grants (or the CIAM account) must be deactivated. The first-login email fallback binds an unbound contact from an email or UPN claim. This is mitigated because A1 keeps self sign-up disabled and invite writes the oid up front (InviteExternalUserEndpoint.cs:140-144).

Org-inherited grants check only the junction's statecode: no sprk_enddate bound, and the organization's own statecode is not checked (ExternalParticipationService.cs:1101-1103). The job that would deactivate grants for inactive orgs and memberships past their end date ships disabled (ExternalAccessModule.cs:371-372). Org grants are also never invalidated per member (GrantExternalAccessEndpoint.cs:501-510), so they rely on the TTL.

Grant rows created outside the BFF (MDA form, Web API, import) bypass DelegationRuleFilter's Write-on-target rule. Dataverse still enforces Create and Append/AppendTo privileges, and a row with no expiry confers nothing, but a dated row with a level does grant CIAM access.

Out of scope for CIAM: MDA, Office add-ins, Teams, Word, AI search and Direct-Office (ADR-028 A1 E-3). The CIAM contact is not a Dataverse principal, and the token authenticates only on /api/v1/external. There are no DefaultPolicy or FallbackPolicy overrides.

Adjacent finding in shared code, workforce plane only (not UC3). The Redis CachedGrantSet does not persist DirectAccessLevel (ExternalParticipationService.cs:1141-1154, 1247-1251, 1263-1267). On a cache hit, workforce Secure suppression therefore treats every grant as org-inherited: a DIRECT grant on a secure record resolves to None for up to 60s after the first miss. Also, a None-rights workforce entry still passes HasProjectAccess membership gates on the project routes.

corrections.claim: STANDING GRANT and ORG-EXPANSION (FR-24/25) are NOT applied to CIAM ... This is still open as design-register C-2 (notes/design-register.md:96).
corrections.problem: C-2 is not open. The design marks it resolved, and the resolution says the standing grant applies to contacts. So this is a designed-but-not-live gap on the CIAM plane, not an open question.
corrections.correction: C-2 was resolved in design: "standing grant applies to organizations, contacts and internal workforce". The code implements the standing-grant and org-expansion terms only in AccessibleRecordSetService.ComposeForContactAsync, which serves WorkforcePrincipal ContactOnly callers. CiamContactPrincipalStrategy never calls it. For CIAM contacts, FR-24/25 is DESIGNED, NOT LIVE. Treat it as a gap against a decided design, not as an undecided register item.
