corrections.claim: The module seam gates on id-set membership ... so such a grant would confer READ through /api/dataverse fetch and record (including child documents and invoices).
corrections.problem: Overstated. A single-record read (/record) of a CHILD module row (document, invoice) always fails closed. IsRecordAccessible checks the record's OWN id against the dimension sets, and for a child module those sets hold parent (project/matter/WA) ids.
corrections.correction: A null-level (None-rights) matter or WA grant confers READ through /api/dataverse/fetch for the root itself and for its child documents and invoices. It confers READ through /api/dataverse/record only for the ROOT record (sprk_matter or sprk_workassignment by own id). /record on sprk_document or sprk_invoice is denied for every caller, whatever their grants.
corrections.evidence: ExternalModuleRegistry.cs:122-128 (remark: "child single-record reads ... fail closed because a child's own id is never in a parent-id set") and 129-144 (IsRecordAccessible compares recordId to dim.AccessibleIds); ExternalAccessModule.cs:244-268 (the document and invoice dimensions are parent lookups).

corrections.claim: Column exposure on the module seam is not narrowed ... the caller-chosen $select at RecordService.cs:68-74 and caller FetchXML attributes.
corrections.problem: The finding is correct, but it leaves out its most concrete consequence and the stale security claims it falsifies. Nothing filters attributes: EvaluateFetchXmlGuard checks only entity names and <link-entity>, so <all-attributes/> or explicit pointer columns are admitted. In-scope sprk_document rows carry SPE Graph pointers and the SharePoint webUrl, written by the external upload path itself.
corrections.correction: A CIAM caller with any document-scope root can fetch sprk_graphdriveid, sprk_graphitemid and sprk_filepath (the SPE webUrl) through POST /api/v1/external/api/dataverse/fetch. It can do the same through /record on root modules for their own columns. This contradicts the file-header invariant "no Graph pointer ever reaches the client" and ExternalProjectDataEndpoints' "Graph pointers are never surfaced on this surface". The impact is disclosure only: a CIAM identity cannot use the pointers against SPE. The comments should still be listed as stale/false alongside the others.
corrections.evidence: ExternalModuleDataEndpoints.cs:26-28 (the "no Graph pointer ever reaches the client" claim) and 502-548 (the guard checks entity identity and link-entity only); FetchService.cs:145-149 (projects every returned attribute); ExternalDataService.cs:252-253, 259-260 (the upload writes sprk_graphitemid, sprk_graphdriveid and sprk_filepath on sprk_document); ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:661 and 724-725 (the "never surfaced" claims).

corrections.claim: All data is read and written app-only by the BFF. (Implied: CIAM writes raise no further access-model issue.)
corrections.problem: Material omission on the WRITE side. Records a CIAM contact creates (document rows, to-dos, calendar events) are POSTed app-only with no ownerid, no RecordOwnershipResolver and no core-ancestor stamp. The other BFF to-do writer (TodoRegardingBuilder) does stamp. So on a Secure project, children created by outside counsel are not placed under the Secure Record BU / owner-team model, and they miss the core-ancestor stamp that internal visibility relies on.
corrections.correction: Add this caveat: CIAM-created children land owned by the BFF application user (the BU default, per I-6) and without the core-ancestor stamp (I-1). Secure child isolation is unimplemented anyway (I-2), so a document uploaded by an external contact to a secure project is not isolated at the Dataverse level. Depending on the reader's path, it may also be invisible or mis-scoped for internal users.
corrections.evidence: ExternalDataService.cs:248-255 (document create payload), 589-596 (event), 736-765 (to-do): no ownerid and no core-ancestor field. A Grep for CoreAncestor or RecordOwnershipResolver finds 0 hits in Infrastructure/ExternalAccess and Api/ExternalAccess, while Services/Workspace/TodoRegardingBuilder.cs does reference CoreAncestorResolver. docs/architecture/DATAVERSE-WRITE-PATH-ARCHITECTURE.md:124-129 (I-1 unstamped create paths, I-2 secure children not isolated, I-6 BFF-created records land in root BU).

corrections.claim: Caveat list on what the CIAM path checks: contact statecode unchecked; org statecode and junction end-date unchecked (the list implies root records are otherwise gated).
corrections.problem: Omission: nothing on the CIAM path checks the ROOT record's own statecode. Grant rows are filtered on the grant's statecode and expiry only, and the project read queries by id alone. A project, matter or WA deactivated natively in Dataverse, rather than through POST /close-project (which deactivates the grants), stays fully readable and writable by its grant holders.
corrections.correction: Add this caveat: root-record deactivation does not revoke CIAM access. Only deactivating or expiring the sprk_externalrecordaccess rows does, and that is what ProjectClosureEndpoint does. Native deactivation of a project or matter leaves CIAM access live.
corrections.evidence: ExternalParticipationService.cs:61-62 (the grant filter has the grant statecode only); ExternalDataService.cs:181-188 and 197-198 (GetProjectsAsync and GetProjectByIdAsync filter by id only and return statecode for display); ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:273, 290, 322 (the gates are HasProjectAccess membership only).

corrections.claim: No DefaultPolicy or FallbackPolicy override exists, so a CIAM token gets 401 on every other route.
corrections.problem: Overstated. Having no FallbackPolicy also means routes marked AllowAnonymous, and any route lacking RequireAuthorization, accept any caller regardless of token.
corrections.correction: A CIAM token authenticates only on /api/v1/external/* (ExternalCollaboration). It gets 401 on every other route that requires authorization under the default scheme. Anonymous routes (health/ping, config, registration, webhook receivers, the Event Grid ingress) are reachable by anyone, including a CIAM caller, because they require no identity.
corrections.evidence: Grep for AllowAnonymous: EndpointMappingExtensions.cs:62, 69, 75, 78, 112, 116, 129; ConfigEndpoints.cs:61, 84; RegistrationEndpoints.cs:23; CommunicationEndpoints.cs:401; AcsEventGridEndpoints.cs:31; ComposeSyncEndpoints.cs:43; ConsentCallbackEndpoint.cs:71; OfficeEndpoints.cs:85 and 178.

corrections.claim: PLAUSIBLE, not observed live: ≤60s grant/revoke latency with invalidation that misses ... Adjacent finding ... a DIRECT grant on a secure record resolves to None for up to 60s after the first miss.
corrections.problem: (a) The invalidation miss is structural, not merely plausible. The resolver's own plane selection assumes a CIAM token's tid equals Ciam:TenantId, which is a separate tenant from the admin's workforce tid, so the keys can never coincide. The only remaining uncertainty is whether a CIAM entry exists at all, which requires tid to be present. (b) The adjacent DirectAccessLevel cache bug is understated. It is not a single 60s window: every cache miss recomputes correctly and re-caches, and every hit for the next 60s returns the broken shape. Under steady use, most requests get the wrong answer.
corrections.correction: (a) Revocation and grant changes for a CIAM contact take effect only at TTL expiry whenever the CIAM token carries tid. Explicit invalidation from /grant, /revoke and /set-record-share-expiry cannot reach the CIAM entry by construction. (b) On the workforce plane, a direct grant on a secure record resolves to None on every cache HIT (every request except the one that misses in each 60s cycle), not just once.
corrections.evidence: CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:302-309 (tid == Ciam:TenantId ⇒ CIAM plane); ExternalParticipationService.cs:193-202 and 290-296 (cache keyed on the current request's tid); GrantExternalAccessEndpoint.cs:500, 511-514 and RevokeExternalAccessEndpoint.cs:197, 206-210 (the admin's tid); TenantCache.cs:257-258 (the key includes the tenant); ExternalParticipationService.cs:201-208 (a hit returns cached), 217-224 (a miss re-caches), 1141-1154 and 1247-1251 (DirectAccessLevel not persisted).

corrections.claim: Grant-read failure fails closed but sticks. A failed Dataverse query returns ExternalGrantSet.Empty ... and GetGrantSetAsync still caches it for 60s.
corrections.problem: Incomplete. A PARTIAL failure is also cached and never surfaced: when the direct-grant query succeeds but the org-membership or org-grant read faults, the direct-only set is cached for 60s. Also, the org junction's lookup names are flagged in code as an unverified assumption, and the claim that each row targets exactly one root is a data assumption the code does not enforce.
corrections.correction: Add three points. (1) An org-read fault silently drops every org-inherited grant, and that narrowed set is cached for 60s. (2) The code itself says the sprk_contactorganization lookup names (_sprk_contact_value / _sprk_organization_value) must be "confirmed against the created junction schema"; if they are wrong, Term 3 contributes nothing, fail-closed and silent. (3) The partitioning uses independent Where clauses, so a row with more than one root lookup populated would grant every root it names. The "exactly one root" property rests on live data, not on code.
corrections.evidence: ExternalParticipationService.cs:914, 1023-1025, 1044-1059 and 1127-1131 (org faults → empty list, direct rows kept); 221-224 (cached); 1092-1094 (the "NOTE: assumes the junction's lookup logical names ... confirm against the created junction schema"); 871-907 (independent partition filters) and 840-841 (the comment relies on "verified live").

corrections.claim: The first-login email fallback binds an unbound contact from an email or UPN claim. This is mitigated because A1 keeps self sign-up disabled and invite writes the oid up front.
corrections.problem: The main mitigation is a tenant configuration stated in ADR text (isSignUpAllowed=false), not something the BFF enforces or can verify. The trace also leaves out that the email query uses $top=1 with no $orderby. Where duplicate contacts share emailaddress1, which contact gets bound on first login is arbitrary, and all later access follows that contact's grants.

trace.use_case: UC4: a SYSTEM USER (a Dataverse systemuser signed in with an internal Entra workforce token) opens or acts on a SECURE record (sprk_issecure = true). The main case is sprk_project, the only entity with a code path that isolates it. sprk_matter and sprk_workassignment also carry the flag but have no isolation code. The planes are traced separately: (P1) the model-driven app, native Dataverse; (P2) BFF routes for Office and internal surfaces, which ask Dataverse as the caller via OBO or impersonation; (P3) the SPA/Teams workforce plane (/api/v1/external/*), where the BFF itself composes access and never calls Dataverse as the user.
trace.identity_resolution:
P1 (model-driven app): the Dataverse session is the systemuser. No BFF code is involved.
P2 (Office and internal BFF), four routes:
(a) AuthorizationService passes the bearer token through (AuthorizationService.cs:76-80, 223-225). DataverseAccessDataSource.GetRecordAccessAsync exchanges it via OBO (DataverseAccessDataSource.cs:419). It then maps the token's oid to a systemuser with an explicit per-request token, filtering systemusers on azureactivedirectoryobjectid eq oid (426, 533-534). The oid comes from CallerResolution.ResolveObjectId (ContainerDocumentAuthorizationFilter.cs:198).
(b) CallerRecordAccessProbe exchanges the caller token via OBO (CallerRecordAccessProbe.cs:224-225, 300-308). It then calls WhoAmI() on the OBO token (357-381), so the principal is the credential itself, not data.
(c) /api/office/search/entities uses ICallerSystemUserResolver and sends the MSCRMCallerID header (OfficeService.cs:69, 84; master's task 062).
(d) The three /api/office/communications routes use IDataverseUserClient (OBO), registered unconditionally (SpaarkeCore.cs:94-95).
P3 (SPA/Teams): CallerPrincipalResolver.DeterminePlane chooses Workforce when iss is not *.ciamlogin.com and tid differs from Ciam:TenantId (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:293-313). WorkforcePrincipalResolver reads the oid claim (WorkforcePrincipalResolver.cs:99), then MembershipEndpoints.ResolveSystemUserIdAsync maps oid to systemuserid app-only (114-116). The linked contact comes from IdentityNormalizationService (sprk_primarycontact / AAD cross-ref, 127). If there is no linked contact, a verified email is matched to an UNBOUND contact (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:1019-1027 → ExternalParticipationService.cs:327-348).
trace.mechanism_one_line: Provisioning moves a secure sprk_project into ownership of the memberless default owner team of the one "Secure Record" business unit. People then get in only through explicit POA shares, or through a role whose depth reaches that BU (in practice, admins). The model-driven app and the BFF OBO/impersonation routes use Dataverse's own answer. The SPA/Teams workforce plane still pattern-matches membership app-only: it never sees POA shares and does not apply Secure isolation to the membership term.
trace.what_grants_access:
1. An explicit POA share on the secure row. There are two ways to get one:
   - At provisioning: a share to the creator, who is identified from their own token via OBO WhoAmI (ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:705-731), plus best-effort shares to named SharePrincipalIds (748-771).
   - Later, through POST /api/v1/external-access/share-user (InternalShareEndpoints.cs:148, 344-346). The caller needs Write on the record, probed via OBO (DelegationRuleFilter.cs:86; ExternalAccessEndpoints.cs:123-126). The level granted is cut down to the caller's own rights (InternalShareEndpoints.cs:276-303; RecordShareLevels.cs:132-150).
2. A security role whose read depth reaches the Secure Record BU: Global (System Administrator), or Deep held at an ancestor BU. This is environment configuration; no code enforces it.
3. Ownership. After provisioning the owner is the Secure Record BU's default owner team (ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:373-379, 609-616), which is kept memberless by design, so ownership gives no person access.
4. On P3 only, BFF-computed terms (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:997-1062):
   - ADR-034 membership on ownerid / owningteam / owningbusinessunit (MembershipResolverService.cs:595-596, 688-692) plus reviewed Contact/Organization lookups in the access-conferring registry, bound to the user's derived contact (MembershipResolverService.cs:864-930). Secure does not suppress this term.
   - The user's linked contact's own sprk_externalrecordaccess grants. On a secure record only the DIRECT level counts; org-inherited grants are suppressed (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:237-256, 1059-1062).
trace.access_level_granted:
P1/P2: exactly what Dataverse's RetrievePrincipalAccess returns, mapped by DataverseAccessRightsMapper.cs:63-70. AssignAccess maps to None.
- Creator's provisioning share: Read, Write, Append, AppendTo, Share (ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:169).
- Named colleagues at provisioning: Collaborate = Read, Write, Append, AppendTo (ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:181; RecordShareLevels.cs:59).
- "+ User" shares: View Only = Read; Collaborate; Full Access = Collaborate + Delete (RecordShareLevels.cs:51-62). Never Share or Assign, and never more than the sharer holds.
- Admins: everything their role gives.
- BFF gates: OperationAccessRule allows when OperationAccessPolicy.HasRequiredRights passes (OperationAccessRule.cs:49). Examples:
  - Office save needs AppendTo (EntityAccessFilter.cs:260-266).
  - Container document listing needs Read on the owning secure record (ContainerDocumentAuthorizationFilter.cs:299-306).
  - If RPA fails on the DataverseAccessDataSource path only, the fallback probe grants at most Read (DataverseAccessDataSource.cs:436-449).
P3:
- A membership hit gives the constant Read|Write|Create (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:288-289), whatever the POA share level.
- A contact grant gives the DIRECT grant's ExternalAccessLevels rights, combined highest-wins.
- Vetoes then remove entries. On the systemuser plane, membership survives the Restricted veto (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:1090-1094, 391-406).

gaps_or_caveats: ISOLATION DEPENDS ON THE ENVIRONMENT, NOT CODE. Provisioning moves the row into the Secure Record BU, but protection holds only if no non-admin human has Deep read at an ancestor of that BU, or Global read. design.md:306-339 recorded this failing in dev: Spaarke Basic User had Deep at the root BU, and an impersonated read of a secure project succeeded. design.md:367-395 records Fix A as validated by an operator test. The live half of the NFR-05 check runs only when SPAARKE_NFR05_DATAVERSE_URL / SPAARKE_NFR05_REQUIRED are set (SecureBuRoleDepthAssertionTests.cs:50,62). I did not verify the current live state.

System Administrator (Global) humans read every secure record by design (admin allow-list, SecureBuRoleDepthAssertionTests.cs:134-142). A test comment (147-149) says the root BU default team held System Administrator in dev, which would give bulk admin reach. That claim is about environment state and I did not verify it.

ONLY sprk_project IS ISOLATED BY CODE. The only ownerid@odata.bind writes in the BFF are provisioning and unsecure (ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:614, UnsecureProjectEndpoint.cs:176), both on sprk_project. For a secure sprk_matter or sprk_workassignment the flag only affects BFF evaluator suppression and container choice; Dataverse gives it no isolation unless an operator assigns it by hand.

CHILD RECORDS ARE NOT ISOLATED. Nothing assigns sprk_document or the other 17 child entities to the secure team (design.md:581-588; confirmed by the grep above). BFF document gates run RPA against sprk_documents({docId}), the document row owned in the uploader's BU (DocumentAuthorizationFilter.cs:100 -> DataverseAccessDataSource.cs:662-663). So a secure project's document rows are visible to anyone Dataverse lets read that row. Only SPE content placement is protected (RecordContainerResolver.cs:227-266).

P3 OVER-GRANT (plausible; not tested live). The systemuser membership term is not Secure-suppressed (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:1044-1051). Its comment says the Secure BU covers the Dataverse half, but P3 reads are app-only, so the BU gives no protection there. A system user whose linked contact sits in a registry Contact lookup (e.g. sprk_assignedattorney1) on a secure project, with no POA share, gets Read|Write|Create on the SPA/Teams plane while the model-driven app denies them. The same applies to any user whose own BU is the Secure Record BU (owningbusinessunit match, MembershipResolverService.cs:911-916).

P3 UNDER-GRANT. Membership never reads POA shares. The creator and every '+ User' sharee of a provisioned secure project do not see it on the SPA/Teams plane unless they are also matched by a lookup or hold their own contact grant. ADR-028 Amendment A5 (ADR-028:288-290) says systemuser root sets MUST come from Dataverse's impersonated answer, but ImpersonatedRootSetSource is registered and inert (ExternalAccessModule.cs:195-198; the evaluator constructor at AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:708-713 does not take it). InternalShareEndpoints.cs:358-359 invalidates a cache nothing reads.

DEFERRED-ACCESS ESCALATION: the management group is gated only on Write (DelegationRuleFilter.cs:86). (a) A Collaborate sharee, who has Write but no ShareAccess, can share the secure record onward through /share-user up to Collaborate. That contradicts ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:171-174, which says re-sharing stays with the creator. (b) Any Write holder can call /unsecure-project, which honours request.ReassignToSystemUserId unchecked (UnsecureProjectEndpoint.cs:294-295). It reassigns the record app-only to any user, revokes every share and clears the flag. That effectively grants Assign, which ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:166-167 says secure projects deliberately withhold. Both are plausible from reading the code; neither was tested live.

The deny-list veto on P3 does not run for a system user with no linked or email-matched contact (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:608-612). The Restricted veto never removes the membership term (398-401).
Fail direction varies by path:
- AuthorizationService, GetRecordAccessAsync and CallerRecordAccessProbe fail closed to None.
- DataverseAccessDataSource degrades to a Read-only probe when RPA fails (436-449). Reads can still pass while writes are denied.
- Flag reads fail closed to secure+restricted (ExternalParticipationService.cs:603-608).
- teammembership in identity normalization fails soft to empty (MembershipResolverService.cs:589-593).
- RecordContainerResolver treats a masked (field-level security) or null sprk_issecure as non-secure, with only a warning (218-227).
Revocation latency: BFF access snapshots are cached 60s (CachedAccessDataSource.cs:59). P3 membership is cached 5 min (MembershipResolverService.cs:112).

DataverseAccessDataSource.GetUserAccessAsync (the document path) writes the OBO token into the shared _httpClient.DefaultRequestHeaders (293-294) and reuses it for the oid lookup, teams and roles. The typed client is transient (SpaarkeCore.cs:63), so the risk is small. The RPA call itself uses an explicit token.
trace.designed_vs_live_notes:
Designed but not live:
- ADR-028 A5 / FR-20: the P3 systemuser root set should come from Dataverse's impersonated answer. It is still ADR-034 membership (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:994-1002 says task 036 is still open). ImpersonatedRootSetSource is registered but unused (ExternalAccessModule.cs:195-198).
- Access teams, described as "the eventual mechanism" (ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:689-694; design §5.1b), are not built. Per-user POA shares are what actually runs.
- Child-record ownership follow-through is recommended as a separate task (design.md:590-596) and not built.
- The BU restructure and role-depth fix are environment configuration, not code.

corrections.claim: CHILD RECORDS ARE NOT ISOLATED ... BFF document gates run RPA against sprk_documents({docId}), the document row owned in the uploader's BU (DocumentAuthorizationFilter.cs:100 -> DataverseAccessDataSource.cs:662-663).
corrections.problem: This is wrong for every document the BFF creates. The row is not owned in the uploader's BU. DataverseServiceClientImpl.CreateDocumentAsync sets ownerid only when request.OwningTeamId is supplied (DataverseServiceClientImpl.cs:303-306). No caller supplies it: OfficeService.cs:866-877 passes only preAssignedDocumentId. git grep finds no other owningTeamId source. No BFF path writes ownerid on sprk_document, so the row defaults to the BFF application user in the ROOT BU. The code's own comments record this: DataverseServiceClientImpl.cs:294-299 and RecordOwnershipResolver.cs:25-29 say "ALL 512 sprk_document rows sit in root". The trace also misses that master's task-080 fix is designed but not live. IRecordOwnershipResolver would put a document filed against a secure project into the Secure Record BU's team (RecordOwnershipResolver.cs:148-180). It is registered (MetadataServiceExtensions.cs:103) and has ZERO consumers. Its only mentions outside its own file are comments (OfficeDocumentPersistence.cs:253, DataverseServiceClientImpl.cs:301).
corrections.correction: Documents a secure project gets through the BFF (Office save, upload finalization, email attachments, communications, P3 ExternalDataService) are app-user-owned in the root BU. Only documents created client-side through Xrm.WebApi are owned by the uploader. The document-level RPA therefore answers from root-BU ownership. Humans with Deep read at root, or Global, read these rows. Child-BU users, including the project's own POA sharees, get nothing through ownership, because the project share does not extend to the document row unless relationship cascade-share is configured (environment state, not verified). Add task 080 (RecordOwnershipResolver) to designed_vs_live_notes as registered-but-inert.
corrections.evidence: DataverseServiceClientImpl.cs:290-306; OfficeService.cs:866-877; OfficeDocumentPersistence.cs:104-117,126-137,253-257; git grep 'ResolveOwningTeamAsync|IRecordOwnershipResolver' finds only the definition, the registration and comments, in both the merged tree and MERGE_HEAD; the only ownerid writes in src/server that touch sprk_document are DataverseServiceClientImpl.cs:305, and it is conditional.

corrections.claim: (a) AuthorizationService passes the bearer token through (AuthorizationService.cs:76-80, 223-225). DataverseAccessDataSource.GetRecordAccessAsync exchanges it via OBO (DataverseAccessDataSource.cs:419)... explicit per-request token (426, 533-534).

AuthorizationService.cs:76-80 (AuthorizeAsync) and 223-225 (GetCallerAccessAsync) call IAccessDataSource.GetUserAccessAsync, not GetRecordAccessAsync. GetUserAccessAsync is the document-only path: its RPA target is hard-coded to sprk_documents (DataverseAccessDataSource.cs:372-373, 662-663). Its oid lookup does not use an explicit token. It uses the mutated shared DefaultRequestHeaders (293-294, 307, 577-586). The explicit-token, entity-generic GetRecordAccessAsync is reached only through GetCallerRecordAccessAsync (AuthorizationService.cs:281-282).

The only AuthorizationService path that asks about the secure record itself is GetCallerRecordAccessAsync → GetRecordAccessAsync. Its consumers are ContainerDocumentAuthorizationFilter.cs:299-304 and SemanticSearchAuthorizationFilter (scope=entity). Cite 281-282, not 76-80/223-225, for the (a) chain.

The todo route carries master's TodoSourceAccessFilter (OfficeEndpoints.cs:1543), which requires Read, not AppendTo, on each of up to four caller-supplied ids and returns one uniform 403.

corrections.claim: what_grants_access 1: 'At provisioning: a share to the creator, who is identified from their own token via OBO WhoAmI (ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:705-731)'
corrections.problem: The 'creator' is whoever CALLS /provision-project, not the person who created the record. The route is gated only on Write on the not-yet-provisioned project (DelegationRuleFilter.cs:239-241, 86). Before provisioning the project is user-owned in a normal BU, so a BU colleague with Write through role depth can provision it. That colleague receives CreatorAccessRights, which include ShareAccess. The real creator loses ownership to the memberless team and gets NO share unless the caller listed them in SharePrincipalIds, which is best-effort (748-771).
corrections.correction: Add this caveat: the ShareAccess-bearing 'creator' share goes to the provisioning caller. Isolation can strand the actual author, and it hands re-share rights to whichever Write-holder triggers provisioning first. In practice the wizard calls it right after creation, which makes caller = creator the common case, not a guarantee.
corrections.evidence: ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:676-679 ('identified from their own token ... never from the request body'), 705-731, 748-771; DelegationRuleFilter.cs:239-241.

corrections.claim: DEFERRED-ACCESS ESCALATION: ... (a) share-user onward; (b) unsecure-project reassignment (the full list of Write-only escalations)
corrections.problem: The list leaves out /unshare-user. Any Write holder, for example a Collaborate sharee, can revoke ANY user's POA share on the secure record, including the provisioning creator's. There is no rights intersection, no creator or last-writer protection, and no eligibility check. The owner team is memberless by design, so removing the remaining Write-bearing shares leaves the record reachable only by admins: the 'locked box' state task 061 was built to prevent.
corrections.correction: Add (c): /unshare-user (Write-gated only) lets any sharee remove every other sharee, the creator included. On a secure project this can lock out every non-admin human.
corrections.evidence: InternalShareEndpoints.cs:395-475 (UnshareAsync: existence check, strict share read, RevokeAccessAsync; no caller-rights probe); DelegationRuleFilter.cs:267-268, 86; ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:669-674.

corrections.claim: RecordContainerResolver.cs:227-266 -- secure record resolves to its own sprk_containerid or 409s; never the shared fallback. ... Only SPE content placement is protected.
corrections.problem: The resolver trusts whatever value is stamped in the secure record's sprk_containerid (227-228). SecureContainerDecision.Decide returns ResolvedSecure for any non-blank value (SecureContainerDecision.cs:62-70). Nothing checks that the value is a provisioned per-record container. Until task 076 (2026-09-03) the create wizard cascaded the creating user's BU (shared) container into that column, and the code documents this (ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:860-864, 996-1004; SecureContainerDecision.cs:31-35). A secure project created before then and never provisioned therefore resolves as ResolvedSecure to a SHARED container. 'Never the shared fallback' is true only of the fallback variable.
corrections.correction: Say instead: a secure record resolves to whatever sprk_containerid holds, or 409s when it is blank. Legacy unprovisioned secure projects that still carry the old BU-cascade stamp will write into the shared BU container. Also, no code writes sprk_containerid on sprk_matter or sprk_workassignment; the only writer is ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:888. Record-keyed uploads to a secure matter or work assignment therefore fail closed 409 permanently (RecordContainerResolver.cs:244-265; OBOEndpoints.cs:119-136), unless a legacy stamp exists.
corrections.evidence: RecordContainerResolver.cs:227-242; SecureContainerDecision.cs:31-35, 60-71; EntityCreationService.ts:55 (cascade removed by task 076); git grep '["sprk_containerid"] =' → ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:888 only.

corrections.claim: Revocation latency: BFF access snapshots are cached 60s (CachedAccessDataSource.cs:59).
corrections.problem: The claim is too broad. The 60s cache applies only to IAccessDataSource, i.e. the AuthorizationService paths, and it also caches DENIALS, including exception/OBO-failure denials (CachedAccessDataSource.cs:131-134, 208-210). The CallerRecordAccessProbe gates (delegation, /office/save, /office/todo, share-user's re-probe) are NOT cached, so a POA revocation takes effect on them immediately. The probe does add a 400ms+1200ms not-found retry before denying (CallerRecordAccessProbe.cs:95-100, 434-444), which the 'every failure returns None' description leaves out.
corrections.correction: Distinguish the paths. The AuthorizationService/IAccessDataSource snapshots, both grants and denials, can be up to 60s stale. The CallerRecordAccessProbe gates are live, with a replication-lag retry of about 1.6s on 404.
corrections.evidence: CachedAccessDataSource.cs:59, 77-142, 145-213; CallerRecordAccessProbe.cs:95-100, 418-485; SpaarkeCore.cs:100-108.

trace.use_case: UC5: an INTERNAL workforce user who is NOT a Dataverse systemuser but resolves to a contact (a "ContactOnly" workforce principal, e.g. a Teams-host or collaboration-SPA user) accessing a SECURE record (sprk_issecure = true on a sprk_project, sprk_matter or sprk_workassignment root, or on a document, invoice, to-do or event under one).
trace.identity_resolution:
Plane selection: the /api/v1/external group accepts both the Ciam and the default workforce JwtBearer schemes (AuthorizationModule.cs:351-359; ExternalAccessEndpoints.cs:54-57). CallerPrincipalResolver.DeterminePlane chooses Workforce whenever iss does not contain "ciamlogin.com" and tid does not equal Ciam:TenantId (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:293-313). WorkforcePrincipalStrategy then calls WorkforcePrincipalResolver (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:483-487).

Claim to row, all reads APP-ONLY through IDataverseService (no OBO, per ADR-028 A2):
(a) The oid claim (MembershipEndpoints.ExtractAadObjectId) is looked up as systemuser.azureactivedirectoryobjectid == oid AND isdisabled == false (MembershipEndpoints.cs:434-457). No row means "not a systemuser" (WorkforcePrincipalResolver.cs:114-118).
(b) Contact branch: IdentityNormalizationService.TryResolveContactByWorkforceIdentityAsync (IdentityNormalizationService.cs:242-303). The primary path is contact.azureactivedirectoryobjectid == oid with TopCount 1 (lines 535-577). The fallback, used only when the oid match finds nothing, takes the first of the email, preferred_username, upn or ClaimTypes.Email claims (WorkforcePrincipalResolver.cs:220-228) and matches contact.emailaddress1 with TopCount 2. It then applies the no-hijack decision DecideWorkforceEmailMatch (lines 482-531): more than one match, a contact bound to a different oid, or an unreadable binding all deny. An UNBOUND contact resolves, and this path never writes the binding (lines 467-480). A thrown exception denies (WorkforcePrincipalResolver.cs:177-194).
(c) A match produces WorkforcePrincipal Kind=ContactOnly with ContactId anchored (WorkforcePrincipalResolver.cs:196-202). No match is an explicit 403, sdap.access.deny.principal_not_resolved (lines 204-212; strategy lines 489-508).

The contact is then the sole subject for grants, standing grant, organization membership and the deny list in AccessibleRecordSetService.ComposeForContactAsync (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:1114-1120). It is never a Dataverse security principal; ADR-028 A5 lines 329-331 say "a contact is not a security principal and cannot be impersonated".
trace.mechanism_one_line: The BFF decides, working like a policy engine over rows it reads app-only from Dataverse. It unions the caller contact's own sprk_externalrecordaccess grants, its standing-grant membership and org expansion. On a sprk_issecure root it keeps only the DIRECT grant level: org-inherited grants, standing membership and org expansion are suppressed before the highest-wins max. It then applies two post-max vetoes, deny-list then Restricted, and stamps the (recordId → rights) map onto CallerPrincipal. The /api/v1/external handlers gate on that map and read or stream data app-only. Dataverse's Secure business unit, owner team and POA shares are never consulted for this principal.
trace.what_grants_access:
Only one thing reaches a secure record: a DIRECT, personal sprk_externalrecordaccess row that meets all of these conditions:
- _sprk_contact_value = the caller's contact
- statecode 0 and not expired (filter at ExternalParticipationService.cs:61-62)
- targets the secure root through _sprk_project_value, _sprk_matter_value or _sprk_workassignment_value
- a row like this carries DirectAccessLevel = sprk_accesslevel (ExternalParticipationService.cs:871-907)

Things that do NOT reach a secure record:
- Organization-inherited grants, which have DirectAccessLevel = null (ExternalParticipationService.cs:917-941).
- The contact's standing-grant membership, filtered by .Where(!IsSecure) at AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:1270-1277.
- Organization expansion, filtered the same way at AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:1283-1290.
All three are suppressed before the max (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:237-259, 1262-1265).

Documents, invoices, to-dos and events do not have their own grants or secure flag. They are reachable through their parent root's id (the module scope dimensions at ExternalAccessModule.cs:244-292, and the project-id routes in ExternalProjectDataEndpoints).

The grant row itself can only be minted through /api/v1/external-access/grant. The DelegationRuleFilter / CallerRecordAccessProbe there requires the GRANTOR to hold Write on the record, checked by OBO WhoAmI + RetrievePrincipalAccess (CallerRecordAccessProbe.cs:206-238). On a secure record that means a systemuser the Secure BU or a POA share admits. The contact itself can never manage access: a non-systemuser gets AccessRights.None at CallerRecordAccessProbe.cs:230-234.
trace.access_level_granted:
The direct row's own level, mapped by ExternalAccessLevels.ToAccessRights (ExternalCallerContext.cs:207-213):
- ViewOnly = Read
- Collaborate = Read | Create | Write
- FullAccess = Read | Create | Write | Delete (no external route exercises Delete)
- A null level = None

Several direct rows on the same record are unioned highest-wins (ExternalParticipationService.cs:953-961, 1000-1011). A suppressed organization grant cannot outbid a lower direct grant: ViewOnly direct plus Collaborate via the organization yields Read.

Two vetoes run after the max and remove the key entirely:
1. The deny list (sprk_noaccessentry, keyed on the contact or its active organizations) (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:375-378).
2. Restricted (sprk_accesspermission == 100000002). On this plane nothing survives it, so even a direct FullAccess grant is removed (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:391-406, 1298-1301; ExternalParticipationService.cs:521).

How routes enforce the rights:
- Mutating routes gate on the specific right: Create for POST to-dos, events and documents (ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:433-434, 570-571, 797-798), Write for PATCH /todos.
- To-do LIST routes gate on Read (ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:399-401).
- The other project read routes gate only on presence in the map (HasProjectAccess). See the first caveat: a None-rights entry still passes those.

gaps_or_caveats: LIVE DEFECT (secure suppression bypassed on READ). The trigger is a secure root the workforce contact reaches ONLY through an org-inherited grant, or through a matter/WA grant row with a null level. GrantedRightsFor still emits the key, with AccessRights.None (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:237-259; the remark at 232-234 admits 'the id still appears in the map'). Neither veto removes None-valued keys (357-407). WorkforcePrincipalStrategy copies the entry into ProjectAccess, MatterAccess and WorkAssignmentAccess (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:527-547). HasProjectAccess is presence-only (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:161), so the caller passes the gates on GET /projects/{id}, /documents, /documents/{doc}/content (app-only byte stream), /versions, /events, /contacts and /organizations (ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:273,290,322,694,766,823,840), and appears in GET /projects (256). The module grid reads use key membership (ExternalModuleRegistry.cs:129-144, 153-168; ExternalAccessModule.cs:229,250-252,291), so documents and invoices under a secure matter or WA leak the same way. Only the to-do list (Read flag, 399-401) and the mutations (Create/Write) deny correctly. Tests assert RightsFor == None but never Contains == false (AccessibleRecordSetServiceTests.cs:700; UnifiedEvaluatorSeamTests.cs:335), so nothing catches this. Found by reading the code; not reproduced at runtime.

A DISABLED systemuser falls through to the contact plane instead of being denied. The systemuser lookup filters isdisabled == false (MembershipEndpoints.cs:448-451), so a disabled user returns null and WorkforcePrincipalResolver tries the contact branch (153-202). If that person's oid is on a contact, or their email matches an unbound contact, they resolve as ContactOnly and keep every DIRECT grant, including grants on secure records. The comment at MembershipEndpoints.cs:444-447 says null 'surfaces as 401'; that is not true on this path.

The email fallback resolves an UNBOUND contact and deliberately never binds the oid (IdentityNormalizationService.cs:467-480), so every request re-matches by email. 'Verified email' is a claim precedence (email, then preferred_username, then upn; WorkforcePrincipalResolver.cs:220-228), not a verification check. The workforce app is multitenant (ADR-028 A2), so the trust in this match rests on the workforce issuer/tenant validation. I did not trace that validation.

Fail directions. A grant-read failure gives an empty set, which denies and is cached 60s (ExternalParticipationService.cs:857-862, 18). A flag-read failure, or an id missing from the flag read, marks the record secure AND restricted, which removes even a direct grant (fail-closed, ExternalParticipationService.cs:529-534, 583-608). A deny-veto read fault denies all candidates (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:614-625, 664-671). Known hole: a failed org-junction QUERY is swallowed as 'no organizations', which narrows the deny-list organization axis (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:578-590).

Staleness. The grant set is cached 60s per tenant and contact (ExternalParticipationService.cs:189-227). Grant, revoke and closure invalidate the key derived from the grantor's tid. The veto flags are NOT cached, so newly setting sprk_issecure or Restricted takes effect on the next request.

Only the three roots carry sprk_issecure/sprk_accesspermission (ExternalParticipationService.cs:502-508). There is no document-level secure flag: children inherit through the parent-id scope dimensions. For any other entity type the flag read returns an empty map, meaning no veto (lines 549-553).

NOT SUPPORTED on the internal MDA/Office plane. A non-systemuser has no Dataverse identity: the OBO per-record path denies caller_not_a_dataverse_user (DataverseAccessDataSource.cs:426-430), and the delegation probe returns None (CallerRecordAccessProbe.cs:230-234). This is structural. The Dataverse secure model (Secure Record BU, memberless default owner team, POA shares; ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:18-27; RecordShareLevels.cs:14-16) only admits systemusers and teams, and ADR-028 A5 (lines 329-331) says a contact cannot be impersonated. For this principal the BFF's sprk_issecure suppression is the ONLY secure-record control; Dataverse row security is never evaluated.

Out of scope, but the same person on the CIAM plane gets NO secure suppression, no deny list and no Restricted veto. CiamContactPrincipalStrategy builds rights from p.AccessLevel (all sources, org grants included) and RightsFromGrants(grant.AccessLevel) (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:386-388, 402-403, 417-429). The plane asymmetry is worth noting for the CIAM use case.

corrections.claim: access_level_granted: 'The direct row's own level' / what_grants_access: 'Only one thing reaches a secure record: a DIRECT, personal sprk_externalrecordaccess row ... a row like this carries DirectAccessLevel = sprk_accesslevel (ExternalParticipationService.cs:871-907)'.
corrections.problem: This holds only on a grant-set cache miss. The Redis grant-set cache does not store DirectAccessLevel, so after a cache hit it is null for every grant. GrantedRightsFor then maps a secure id to AccessRights.None but keeps the key. The trace names the 60s cache as a staleness issue and misses that the cache changes the answer. Most of the time, a DIRECT grant on a secure root gives None, not the granted level. The failure is silent, and the trace's own presence-only defect makes it worse.
corrections.correction: On a cache miss a direct grant on a secure root yields its level. On a cache hit it yields AccessRights.None, and the key is still present. Cache hits cover the rest of the 60s TTL after any miss or invalidation. They can also happen inside a single request: GetGrantSetAsync runs three times (project, matter, work assignment), the first call's cache write is fire-and-forget, and later calls can hit it (timing-dependent). Effect on a hit: /me reports 'None'; POST to-dos, events and documents and PATCH /todos return 403; to-do lists return 403. The presence-gated reads still pass: project GET, documents, content download, versions, events, contacts, organizations, and the module grids. The systemuser plane's contact-grant term (Term 2) has the same defect. No test covers the cache round trip.
corrections.evidence: ExternalParticipationService.cs:1141-1153 (CacheGrantSetAsync writes only ProjectId/RecordId + AccessLevel); 1242-1251 (CachedParticipation.ToParticipation sets no DirectAccessLevel); 1258-1267 (CachedRootGrant.ToGrant sets none); 208 (a hit returns cached.ToGrantSet()); 18 (60s TTL); 223 (unawaited cache write); 290-296 (key uses the tid claim, which workforce tokens carry). AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:244/250/256 (secure id reads DirectAccessLevel, null maps to None). CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:519-524 (three ComposeAsync calls per request). CacheModule.cs:195 (a real TenantCache is always registered). Every test that sets DirectAccessLevel builds ExternalGrantSet directly (AccessibleRecordSetServiceTests.cs:617-1791; UnifiedEvaluatorSeamTests.cs:156-799), and ExternalParticipationService.cs:1273-1278 itself says unit tests bypass the cache.

corrections.claim: 'The grant row itself can only be minted through /api/v1/external-access/grant. The DelegationRuleFilter / CallerRecordAccessProbe there requires the GRANTOR to hold Write on the record.'
corrections.problem: False in two ways. (1) A second BFF route also mints grants: /invite-and-grant, which calls the same CreateGrantAsync. (2) Grant rows can be created entirely outside the BFF, through a form, the Web API, a flow or an import. The code says this explicitly. The evaluator's read filter does not check who created a row or how, so these rows never pass through DelegationRuleFilter. Only Dataverse's own privileges on sprk_externalrecordaccess (and the lookup Append/AppendTo rights) stand in the way.
corrections.correction: Any active row with _sprk_contact_value = the contact, a sprk_expiresdate on or after today, and a root lookup confers access, whoever created it. The BFF delegation gate (grantor Write via OBO WhoAmI + RetrievePrincipalAccess) applies only to /grant and /invite-and-grant. Rows written directly to Dataverse are limited only by Dataverse privileges on that table. For those rows, the /grant delegation check is not the control on who can admit a workforce contact to a secure record.
corrections.evidence: ExternalAccessEndpoints.cs:153-155 (/invite-and-grant on the admin group); InviteAndGrantExternalUserEndpoint.cs:127 (calls GrantExternalAccessEndpoint.CreateGrantAsync); ExternalParticipationService.cs:88-92 ('users hold Create on sprk_externalrecordaccess, so a row created outside the BFF (a form, the Web API, a flow or an import)'); ExternalAccessReconciliationJob.cs:21-23 (same statement); ExternalParticipationService.cs:61-62 (read filter: contact + statecode + expiry only).

corrections.claim: 'statecode 0 and not expired (filter at ExternalParticipationService.cs:61-62)'.
corrections.problem: Omits two qualifying conditions. The expiry predicate is `sprk_expiresdate ge today`, which also excludes rows with a NULL expiry. An undated grant confers nothing (inverted by ISS-009/D-1). In addition, a PROJECT grant row with a null sprk_accesslevel is dropped entirely, while matter and work-assignment rows with a null level are kept as None-valued keys.
corrections.correction: A qualifying direct row must be statecode 0, carry a non-null sprk_expiresdate on or after today (UTC date), and, for a project, carry a non-null sprk_accesslevel.
corrections.evidence: ExternalParticipationService.cs:85-95 and 108-109 (ExpiryPredicate = 'sprk_expiresdate ge {today}'; null excluded); 872 (project rows require sprk_accesslevel.HasValue); 890-907 (matter/WA rows kept with a nullable level).

corrections.claim: First caveat: the leak trigger is 'a secure root the workforce contact reaches ONLY through an org-inherited grant, or through a matter/WA grant row with a null level' — framed as secure suppression bypassed.
corrections.problem: The null-level matter/WA case has nothing to do with Secure. Such a row has AccessLevel and DirectAccessLevel both null, so it produces a None key on ANY root, secure or not. Keeping the key is a documented choice so that set membership is preserved. The org-inherited case also reaches further than stated: the org path never checks sprk_organization.statecode or sprk_contactorganization.sprk_enddate, and the reconciliation job that would clean these up ships disabled. So a deactivated firm or an ended membership still produces the None key.
corrections.correction: Separate the two cases. The org-inherited grant on a secure root is the Secure-specific leak, and it persists through firm deactivation and ended memberships. The null-level matter/WA row is a general None-key presence leak on every root. Both pass HasProjectAccess and the module key-membership gates. With the cache defect above, the Secure-specific leak widens to direct grants as well.
corrections.evidence: ExternalParticipationService.cs:895-896, 904-905 (null level in both slots); 884-889 and ExternalCallerContext.cs:103-109 (deliberate keep, 'contributes AccessRights.None'); ExternalAccessReconciliationJob.cs:21-27 (no statecode check on the org path; memberships ended by date keep conferring), 48-55 (ships disabled, report-only).

corrections.claim: Identity resolution (b): 'The primary path is contact.azureactivedirectoryobjectid == oid ... The fallback, used only when the oid match finds nothing ... applies the no-hijack decision ... a contact bound to a different oid ... deny'.
corrections.problem: Three material omissions. (1) An oid lookup that throws is swallowed as null, so an oid-lookup fault also drops to the weaker email path. (2) No code under src writes contact.azureactivedirectoryobjectid; the only write of that attribute is systemuser creation, and the email path never binds. Unless makers or an out-of-band process populate it, every workforce contact resolves by email on every request and the no-hijack check has nothing to compare. The code itself logs this as inert. (3) The service says the column 'isn't provisioned in every environment'. Where it is absent, the email query, which selects it, throws and returns null, so every workforce contact is denied and UC5 cannot happen at all in that environment.

The no-hijack guard only works where contact.azureactivedirectoryobjectid is provisioned AND populated outside this codebase. Where the column is not provisioned, the workforce contact plane is unusable.

Separately, the live systemuser query has no try/catch, and WorkforcePrincipalResolver does not guard it, so a Dataverse fault there is an unhandled 500 rather than the auditable deny the contact branch gives.

trace.identity_resolution: Plane: the /api/v1/external group requires AuthPolicies.ExternalCollaboration, which accepts both the "Ciam" scheme and the workforce scheme. The group-level CallerPrincipalAuthorizationFilter calls ICallerPrincipalResolver (ExternalAccessEndpoints.cs:54-57, CallerPrincipalAuthorizationFilter.cs:32-48). CallerPrincipalResolver.DeterminePlane picks CiamContact when the validated token's `iss` contains "ciamlogin.com" OR its `tid` equals config Ciam:TenantId (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:293-313). Claim-to-row mapping: CiamContactPrincipalStrategy reads `oid` (or the objectidentifier URI claim) plus preferred_username/upn/email (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:345-350) and calls ExternalParticipationService.ResolveExternalContactAsync (ExternalParticipationService.cs:314-361). That method takes `oid` and does an app-only lookup of contact.sprk_externalobjectid (ResolveContactByOidAsync :366-398); a match is authoritative. Otherwise it falls back to a first-login match on emailaddress1 and binds the oid onto that contact only if the contact has no oid yet (:339-348). A contact already bound to a DIFFERENT oid is refused, so a shared email cannot hijack it (:350-360). With no oid and no email the result is 401 (:352-360). An unresolved contact gets 403 sdap.access.deny.contact_not_found (:366-373). The resolved row is a Dataverse `contact`. It is never a systemuser, so it is not a Dataverse security principal (SystemUserId = null at CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:394).
trace.mechanism_one_line: The BFF reads the contact's own active, unexpired sprk_externalrecordaccess rows plus the org-grant rows inherited through active sprk_contactorganization memberships (app-only, cached 60s). It folds them highest-wins into CallerPrincipal (recordId -> AccessRights) and checks each route by id-in-set, plus Create or Write for mutations. It never reads sprk_issecure or sprk_accesspermission, and never runs the Secure / Restricted / deny-list veto pipeline on this plane. So "secure" has no effect on a CIAM caller's access, only on where uploads are stored.
trace.what_grants_access: An active (statecode 0), unexpired (sprk_expiresdate >= today UTC; a null expiry now grants NOTHING) sprk_externalrecordaccess row. It can be either (a) keyed to the contact (_sprk_contact_value = contactId), or (b) an ORGANIZATION grant row (contact empty, _sprk_organization_value = an org the contact actively belongs to via sprk_contactorganization statecode 0) (ExternalParticipationService.cs:61-72, 108-109, 846-848, 1020-1060, 1096-1132). Each row targets exactly one root: sprk_project, sprk_matter or sprk_workassignment. Child records (documents, invoices, to-dos, events) are reachable only through an accessible root. The rows are written by POST /api/v1/external-access/grant (or /invite-and-grant) by an internal user. DelegationRuleFilter requires that user to hold Write on the target record, checked AS THE CALLER through OBO WhoAmI + RetrievePrincipalAccess (ExternalAccessEndpoints.cs:123-126, DelegationRuleFilter.cs:158-177, CallerRecordAccessProbe.cs:206-238). On a secure record, the internal user's Write normally comes from the explicit POA share that provisioning gives the creator (CollaborateRights + ShareAccess, ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:169, 726-730), because the Secure Record BU's owner team has no members. The grant endpoint does NOT check sprk_issecure on the root. It will write a per-contact grant OR an organization grant on a secure record without distinction (GrantExternalAccessEndpoint.cs:84-93, 596-620, 655-705).
trace.access_level_granted: sprk_accesslevel on the grant row maps through ExternalAccessLevels.ToAccessRights (ExternalCallerContext.cs:207-213): ViewOnly (100000000) = Read; Collaborate (100000001) = Read|Create|Write; FullAccess (100000002) = Read|Create|Write|Delete. Null or an unknown value = None. Across duplicate rows and direct plus org-inherited rows, the HIGHEST level wins (ExternalParticipationService.cs:953-976; CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:417-429 ORs duplicates). The CIAM strategy uses the EFFECTIVE `AccessLevel`, which includes org-inherited rows, and never the `DirectAccessLevel` (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:386-388, 402-403). So on a secure record a contact receives the full org-inherited level. Enforcement is per route. Read routes on ExternalProjectDataEndpoints (GET project, documents, download, versions, events, contacts, organizations) gate only on set membership, HasProjectAccess (any level) (ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:273, 290, 322, 694, 766, 823, 840). To-do list requires Read; to-do/event/document create requires Create; to-do PATCH requires Write (ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:399-401, 433-440, 570-582, 797-804, 897-909). Module-host reads gate on the record id being in the principal's id sets (ExternalModuleDataEndpoints.cs:267-274; ExternalAccessModule.cs:224-292). All data then comes back APP-ONLY: ExternalDataService managed-identity token (ExternalDataService.cs:13, 1102), RecordService over the privileged ServiceClient (RecordServiceExtensions.cs:15), and SPE bytes via app-only SpeFileStore.DownloadFileAsync (ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:344-349).

gaps_or_caveats: The secure flag does not change anything for a CIAM caller. CiamContactPrincipalStrategy (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:375-404) never reads sprk_issecure or sprk_accesspermission and never calls AccessibleRecordSetService. The task 037/039 veto pipeline therefore runs only on the workforce plane.

FR-22 is not enforced on the CIAM plane. The spec (spec.md:85) says Secure suppresses org-expansion terms 'for every principal kind'. Here the org-inherited grant level is used unsuppressed (AccessLevel, not DirectAccessLevel, at CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:386-388, 402-403). Scenario: an org grant on a secure project (GrantExternalAccessEndpoint allows it) gives EVERY active CIAM member of that org access to the secure project at the org's level.

FR-21 is not enforced on the CIAM plane. The spec (spec.md:84) says Restricted 'denies ALL contact principals regardless of grant source'. A CIAM contact with a grant on a sprk_accesspermission=Restricted record keeps full access.

FR-23 is not enforced on the CIAM plane. The spec (spec.md:86) makes the deny list a veto after the max. A CIAM contact on the No Access List (contact or organization key) keeps access through any grant.

The same person gets different answers depending on plane. The same contact authenticating with a WORKFORCE token (Teams, contact-only) goes through ComposeForContactAsync, which DOES apply Secure suppression, the deny list and Restricted (AccessibleRecordSetService.cs:1256-1301). Via CIAM they do not.

No test pins the CIAM plane's behaviour on secure, restricted or denied records: CallerPrincipalResolverTests.cs has no matches for secure, restricted, veto, org grant or DirectAccessLevel. investigation/01-spa-plane.md:77 already noted that the gate is only invoked from the workforce strategy.

Read routes gate on membership, not Read. HasProjectAccess returns true for any listed project (ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:273, 290, 322, 694, 766, 823, 840). On the CIAM plane a project entry always has a level, because null-level project rows are dropped (ExternalParticipationService.cs:872). Matter/WA rows with a null level are KEPT with Rights=None (:890-907), so they still enter AccessibleMatterIds / AccessibleWorkAssignmentIds and are readable through the module-host id-set scoping. The code comment says every dev row carries a level (ExternalCallerContext.cs:107-109).

Dataverse's native model has no effect on a CIAM caller. The Secure Record BU, the memberless default owner team and the POA shares only govern internal Dataverse principals. Every CIAM read is app-only (ExternalDataService.cs:13; RecordServiceExtensions.cs:15 'privileged ServiceClient'; app-only SpeFileStore), so a secure project is exactly as reachable as a non-secure one once a grant row exists.

Fail directions: contact not resolved means 403. A grant-query fault or non-success means an EMPTY grant set, so no access (fail-closed) (ExternalParticipationService.cs:857-862, 989-993). An org-membership or org-grant fault means no org contribution (fail-closed for the additive term). A cache read error falls through to Dataverse. There is no veto pipeline to fail in either direction on this plane.

Revocation is probably stale for up to 60s on the CIAM plane. The grant cache key is `tenant:{tid}:external-access-grant:{contactId}:v4` (TenantCache.cs:257-258). A CIAM request caches under the CIAM `tid`, but /grant and /revoke invalidate under the internal operator's WORKFORCE `tid` (RevokeExternalAccessEndpoint.cs:206-208, 315-316; GrantExternalAccessEndpoint.cs:500-515). So invalidation misses the CIAM entry, and a revoked CIAM contact keeps access until the 60s TTL expires. This is inferred from code and not verified live.

Cross-plane defect found along the way (not on the UC6 path): the grant cache does not carry DirectAccessLevel. CachedParticipation.ToParticipation and CachedRootGrant.ToGrant (ExternalParticipationService.cs:1247-1251, 1263-1267) rebuild grants with DirectAccessLevel=null, and CacheVersion stayed at 4 after task 037 added the field. On a workforce-plane cache HIT, a secure record's DIRECT grant becomes None rights with the id still present. HasProjectAccess stays true while Create/Write are denied, so the answer is correct on a miss and wrong on a hit — the same shape as the defect that task 032's comment warns about.

Grant creation does not check sprk_issecure. Any internal user holding Write on a secure record (normally the creator via the POA share, who also has ShareAccess) can mint per-contact OR organization grants on it. Nothing requires the grant to be per-contact on a secure record.

Upload to a secure project goes to that project's own container, derived server-side. If the secure project has no container, RecordContainerResolver throws 409 secure_record_container_missing (RecordContainerResolver.cs:244-265); the handler returns that status, and the 422 branch covers Unresolved. Upload exists only on /projects/{id}/documents, not on matter or WA roots.

Stale comments: ExternalDataService.cs:16-17 still says access is gated by ExternalCallerAuthorizationFilter (replaced by CallerPrincipalAuthorizationFilter). ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:74-76 says 'nothing yet READS the container this endpoint records', but RecordContainerResolver now reads sprk_containerid on the external upload path (ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:598).
trace.designed_vs_live_notes:
LIVE path: token -> ExternalCollaboration policy -> CallerPrincipalAuthorizationFilter -> DeterminePlane=CiamContact -> CiamContactPrincipalStrategy -> ExternalParticipationService (oid-bound contact; app-only grant rows plus org-inherited grant rows; 60s tid-keyed cache) -> CallerPrincipal (recordId -> rights) -> per-route membership/Create/Write checks in ExternalProjectDataEndpoints and ExternalModuleDataEndpoints -> app-only Dataverse and SPE reads. This follows ADR-028 A1: broker-only, no OBO on the external path (ADR-028 lines 48-50, 123).

DESIGNED but NOT reaching this plane: the three task 037/039 vetoes (FR-21 Restricted, FR-22 Secure pre-max suppression, FR-23 deny list) are implemented and tested, but live only in AccessibleRecordSetService (ApplyVetoPipeline :357-407; GrantedRightsFor isSecure :237-256; ComposeForContactAsync :1256-1301). That service is reached only from WorkforcePrincipalStrategy. The CIAM strategy's own doc says it is the 'EXISTING external-SPA resolution, unchanged' (CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:316-321). The spec wording says FR-21/22 apply to 'all contact principals' / 'every principal kind' (spec.md:84-85), so the CIAM plane is a spec gap, not a deliberate exclusion that any code or ADR records.

REGISTERED-BUT-INERT and irrelevant to UC6: ImpersonatedRootSetSource / ADR-028 A5 (ExternalAccessModule.cs:181-198). It is registered, has no consumer, and applies to WorkforcePrincipalKind.SystemUser only (ADR-028 line 329: the CIAM/contact plane derivation is untouched).

Secure Record provisioning (ProvisionProjectEndpoint: Secure Record BU owner team plus creator POA share plus own SPE container) is live. For a CIAM contact, though, it only affects (a) who can issue the grant: the DelegationRuleFilter OBO Write check, which Dataverse decides natively for the GRANTER, and (b) which container an upload lands in. The CIAM contact's own access decision is made entirely by the BFF from grant rows. Dataverse never evaluates the contact.

Net: UC6 IS SUPPORTED, by explicit grant, with BFF-decided access at the grant row's level. The secure flag does NOT narrow CIAM access: org-inherited grants, Restricted records and deny-list entries are all unenforced on this plane.

corrections.claim: identity_resolution: 'With no oid and no email the result is 401 (:352-360). An unresolved contact gets 403 sdap.access.deny.contact_not_found (:366-373).' This is cited in a sentence where every other bare line number refers to ExternalParticipationService.cs.
corrections.problem: Wrong file. In ExternalParticipationService.cs, lines 352-360 are the refusal when an oid does not match, and lines 366-398 are ResolveContactByOidAsync. The 401 and the 403 are both issued in the strategy.
corrections.correction: The 401 for missing claims is at CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:352-360 and the 403 contact_not_found is at CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:366-373. ExternalParticipationService.ResolveExternalContactAsync only returns null (EPS:328-330, 334-336, 357-360).
corrections.evidence: CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:352-359 (Status401Unauthorized, 'missing required user identity claims'); CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:366-372 (Forbidden 'sdap.access.deny.contact_not_found'); ExternalParticipationService.cs:350-360 (the oid-mismatch refusal) and :366-398 (ResolveContactByOidAsync).

corrections.claim: what_grants_access / designed_vs_live: 'On a secure record, the internal user's Write normally comes from the explicit POA share that provisioning gives the creator ... because the Secure Record BU's owner team has no members'; 'The Secure Record BU, the memberless default owner team and the POA shares only govern internal Dataverse principals'. ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:726-730 is cited as 'the only human path in'.
corrections.problem: This applies project-only machinery to all three secure roots that UC6 names. The BFF provisions ONLY sprk_project. No provision path exists for sprk_matter or sprk_workassignment, so a secure matter or WA gets no Secure Record BU owner, no creator POA share and no own container. Setting sprk_issecure=true on a project also does not mean it was provisioned: provisioning is a separate call that the client triggers. That the owner team has no members is an environment assumption stated only in comments; nothing in code checks it (a Dataverse BU default team contains that BU's users). 'Only human path' also ignores roles with Organization-depth privilege and the named colleagues shared at provisioning.
corrections.correction: The Secure Record BU, the owner team, the POA share and the own container exist only for PROVISIONED secure projects. For a secure matter or WA, the granter's Write comes from ordinary Dataverse BU and role depth. A secure project that was never provisioned also stays in its creator's BU. Named colleagues (SharePrincipalIds) and any user with Organization-depth Write can also reach a provisioned secure project.
corrections.evidence: ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:80 (ProjectEntitySet = "sprk_projects"), :207 (only /provision-project), :279-284, :747-772 (named principals shared at CollaboratorAccessRights). A grep for provision-matter, ProvisionMatter and provision-workassignment across Sprk.Bff.Api finds nothing. There is no code check that the owner team has no members (only comments at :670-671).

corrections.claim: what_grants_access / gaps: 'Any internal user holding Write on a secure record (normally the creator via the POA share, who also has ShareAccess) can mint per-contact OR organization grants on it.'
corrections.problem: This understates who can mint grants. ShareAccess is never checked: DelegationRuleFilter requires only Write. Provisioning deliberately withholds ShareAccess from named colleagues so that 're-sharing stays with the creator so the access list cannot widen through a chain nobody reviewed'. Those colleagues still hold Write (Collaborate), so they can mint per-contact AND org-wide external grants on the secure project, and the intended restriction is defeated for CIAM access. /grant also does not intersect the requested level with the caller's own rights, whereas /share-user does.
corrections.correction: Anyone with Write on the root can mint external grants at any level (including FullAccess and organization grants) to CIAM contacts, whether or not they hold ShareAccess. That includes Collaborate-level colleagues shared at provisioning or later through /share-user. The practical effect of FullAccess (Delete) is nil only because /api/v1/external has no delete route.
corrections.evidence: DelegationRuleFilter.cs:86 (RequiredRight = AccessRights.Write) and :170. A grep for ShareAccess in Api/ExternalAccess matches only ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:164-173 (comments and constants). ProvisionProjectEndpoint.cs:171-181 (CollaboratorAccessRights = CollaborateRights, without ShareAccess). RecordShareLevels.cs:59 (CollaborateRights includes WriteAccess). GrantExternalAccessEndpoint.cs:95-97 (validates only Enum.IsDefined). InternalShareEndpoints.cs:261-290 ('You may grant only what you hold' intersection, which is absent from /grant).

corrections.claim: what_grants_access: 'The rows are written by POST /api/v1/external-access/grant (or /invite-and-grant) by an internal user. DelegationRuleFilter requires that user to hold Write on the target record'.
corrections.problem: Incomplete. The code itself records that sprk_externalrecordaccess rows can be created outside the BFF (a form, the Web API, a flow or an import) because users hold Create on the table. Those rows never pass through DelegationRuleFilter; only native Dataverse privileges gate them. The CIAM read path honours any such row that is active and carries a sprk_expiresdate of today or later.
corrections.correction: The BFF grant endpoints are the product path, not the only path. A row written directly in Dataverse with a future expiry grants CIAM access to a secure root with no BFF delegation check. Since task 107 only an undated row confers nothing.
corrections.evidence: ExternalParticipationService.cs:88-92 ('users hold Create on sprk_externalrecordaccess, so a row created outside the BFF (a form, the Web API, a flow or an import) can still omit it'); ExternalAccessReconciliationJob.cs:21-22 (same statement); ExternalParticipationService.cs:61-62 and 108-109 (the read filter checks only contact, statecode and expiry).

corrections.claim: what_grants_access: an ORGANIZATION grant confers access when the org is 'an org the contact actively belongs to via sprk_contactorganization statecode 0'. Fail directions: 'An org-membership or org-grant fault means no org contribution (fail-closed for the additive term).'
corrections.problem: This omits the caveat that matters most for UC6, where org grants on secure records go unsuppressed on the CIAM plane. 'Active' means only that the junction row has statecode 0. sprk_contactorganization.sprk_enddate is not checked, and neither is sprk_organization.statecode. The code documents both: deactivating a firm revokes nothing, and a membership that ended by date keeps conferring access indefinitely. Membership rows are maker-authored, so they are an access-granting write path with no BFF gate. The reconciliation job that would repair this ships disabled and in report-only mode. Grant and revoke of an org grant also invalidate no cache.
corrections.correction: On the CIAM plane, a contact from a DEACTIVATED firm, or whose firm membership has passed its end date, keeps org-inherited access to secure records until someone deactivates the junction or grant row by hand. Adding a sprk_contactorganization row (with no delegation check) immediately extends every org grant, including grants on secure records, to that contact.
corrections.evidence: ExternalParticipationService.cs:1101-1103 (filter: _sprk_contact_value eq {id} and statecode eq 0 only); :68-72 (the org-grant filter has no org statecode). ExternalAccessReconciliationJob.cs:23-27 ('deactivating a firm revokes nothing ... a membership ended by date keeps conferring indefinitely'; 'Nothing in the repo writes sprk_contactorganization'). ExternalAccessModule.cs:371-372 (AddScheduledJob<ExternalAccessReconciliationJob>(..., enabled: false)). GrantExternalAccessEndpoint.cs:501-510 and RevokeExternalAccessEndpoint.cs:198-205 (no invalidation for org grants).

corrections.claim: identity_resolution treats contact resolution as complete: oid lookup is authoritative, with an email first-login fallback and a no-hijack rule.
corrections.problem: Two caveats that bear on access are missing. (1) Neither the oid lookup nor the email lookup filters on contact statecode, and the grant query is keyed only on the contact FK. A DEACTIVATED contact bound to an oid therefore still resolves, and its active grants still apply, so deactivating the contact revokes nothing on the CIAM plane. (2) The email fallback uses $top=1 on emailaddress1, with no uniqueness check and no verified-email check in code. When several contacts share an email, an arbitrary one is bound. Any CIAM identity whose preferred_username, upn or email claim matches an UNBOUND contact claims it on first login, together with that contact's secure-record grants. Whether preferred_username is verified depends on CIAM tenant configuration, which the code does not enforce.
corrections.correction: State that contact deactivation is not a revocation on this plane. State also that first-login binding relies on the unverified matching of the email claim to emailaddress1 (take the first match) for any contact that has no oid yet.
corrections.evidence: ExternalParticipationService.cs:375 ($filter=sprk_externalobjectid eq '...'&$top=1, no statecode); :423 ($filter=emailaddress1 eq '...'&$top=1, no statecode); :339-347 (binds the oid onto whichever row came back); :61-62 (grants keyed only by _sprk_contact_value); CallerPrincipalResolver.cs:347-350 (preferred_username is tried first).

corrections.claim: designed_vs_live Net: 'UC6 IS SUPPORTED, by explicit grant' (for secure sprk_project / sprk_matter / sprk_workassignment). The gaps list notes only that 'Upload exists only on /projects/{id}/documents'.
corrections.problem: This overstates support for secure matter and WA roots. Document CONTENT and version history are reachable only through project-scoped routes. Those routes require document._sprk_project_value to equal the project id in the route, so a document parented to a matter or WA returns 403. The module host exposes such documents as metadata rows only, and no module-host content route exists.
corrections.correction: For a secure MATTER or WORK ASSIGNMENT, a CIAM contact with a grant can read the root record and document METADATA (through the module host), and can list or create to-dos. It cannot download or version-list the documents on this surface, and cannot upload. Full document access exists only for project roots.
corrections.evidence: ExternalProjectDataEndpoints.cs:107 and :193 (the only content and version routes, both /projects/{id}/documents/{documentId}/...); :333-341 and :702-710 (a document not in the project returns 403); ExternalDataService.cs:297-307 (reads only _sprk_project_value); ExternalAccessModule.cs:244-254 (the documents module is a fetch-scope dimension only); ExternalModuleDataEndpoints.cs:84-123 (fetch, record, metadata and savedquery routes only).

corrections.claim: designed_vs_live: 'the CIAM plane is a spec gap, not a deliberate exclusion that any code or ADR records.'
corrections.problem: The wording is off in both directions. It is not a SPEC gap: the spec covers the CIAM plane, and the implementation does not conform. Task 037 is marked completed with the title 'for every principal kind', a goal of 'on every plane' and a step 3 of 'excluded on BOTH planes', yet its relevant-files list omits CallerPrincipalResolver.cs. Design §4.2 says 'Types 2 and 3 are identical on record permission; they differ only by credential.' Conversely, code and the ADR DO record a deliberate freeze of CIAM behaviour ('unchanged', 'byte-for-byte'). That freeze predates FR-21/22/23 and now collides with them. The collision itself is what nobody recorded.
corrections.correction: Call it an implementation non-conformance with spec FR-21/22/23 and design §4.2. Task 037 claims every-plane scope it did not deliver. corrections.problem: This omits that the fault result is CACHED. GetGrantSetAsync caches whatever QueryGrantSetAsync returns, including ExternalGrantSet.Empty from a fault. corrections.correction: Fail-closed, but sticky: a faulted or partial grant read is cached for 60s under the caller's tid.
